descriptionHtml:
SMBC Group is a top-tier global financial group. Headquartered in Tokyo and with a 400-year history, SMBC Group offers a diverse range of financial services, including banking, leasing, securities, credit cards, and consumer finance. The Group has more than 130 offices and 80,000 employees worldwide in nearly 40 countries. Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc. (SMFG) is the holding company of SMBC Group, which is one of the three largest banking groups in Japan. SMFG’s shares trade on the Tokyo, Nagoya, and New York (NYSE: SMFG) stock exchanges.

In the Americas, SMBC Group has a presence in the US, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Peru. Backed by the capital strength of SMBC Group and the value of its relationships in Asia, the Group offers a range of commercial and investment banking services to its corporate, institutional, and municipal clients. It connects a diverse client base to local markets and the organization’s extensive global network. The Group’s operating companies in the Americas include Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. (SMBC), SMBC Nikko Securities America, Inc., SMBC Capital Markets, Inc., SMBC MANUBANK, JRI America, Inc., SMBC Leasing and Finance, Inc., Banco Sumitomo Mitsui Brasileiro S.A., and Sumitomo Mitsui Finance and Leasing Co., Ltd.

Job Summary

As a Sr. Cyber Security Analyst, you will play a key role in protecting SMBC Group by helping detect, investigate, and respond to cyber threats. You will work within the Security Operations Center (SOC) to strengthen monitoring, incident response, threat hunting, and detection capabilities across a global technology environment.

In this role, you will analyze security events, identify root causes, improve detection coverage, and help enhance security controls. You will also contribute to initiatives that advance the SOC’s capabilities through automation, threat intelligence, purple teaming, digital forensics, and incident response. This is an opportunity to work with modern security technologies, expand your expertise, and directly influence how we defend the organization.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

  • Monitor, investigate, and respond to security alerts, incidents, and suspicious activity across the enterprise.
  • Lead technical investigations to determine root cause, assess impact, and support containment and remediation efforts.
  • Conduct proactive threat hunting activities to identify emerging threats and security gaps.
  • Maintain and enhance monitoring, detection, and incident response playbooks and procedures.
  • Partner with detection engineering and security automation teams to improve visibility, reduce false positives, and strengthen response processes.
  • Evaluate adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) and validate the organization's ability to detect and respond to them.
  • Support the implementation, management, and optimization of security tools and platforms.
  • Contribute to projects and initiatives that improve SOC operations, incident response capabilities, and overall security maturity.

POSITION SPECIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of cybersecurity experience, preferably in a SOC, CSIRT, DFIR, or incident response environment.
  • Experience investigating security incidents and analyzing complex threat activity.
  • Experience documenting investigations, findings, and recommendations clearly and accurately.
  • Strong understanding of security monitoring, incident detection, investigation, containment, and response processes.
  • Knowledge of the MITRE ATT&CK framework, Cyber Kill Chain, and related threat analysis methodologies.
  • Experience working with security technologies such as SIEM, EDR, NDR, XDR, and UEBA platforms.
  • Strong knowledge of Windows and Linux operating systems.
  • Experience with Active Directory and identity-related security concepts.
  • Working knowledge of cloud technologies and cloud security principles.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a results-focused environment.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound decisions during security investigations.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience in threat hunting, digital forensics, purple teaming, detection engineering, security automation, or threat intelligence.
  • Experience developing or tuning security detections and response workflows.
  • Professional certifications such as GCIH, GNFA, GCFA, CEH, OSCP, CISSP, or equivalent.
  • Experience working in a global enterprise or highly regulated environment, including financial services.

SMBC’s employees participate in a Hybrid workforce model that provides employees with an opportunity to work from home, as well as, from an SMBC office. SMBC requires that employees live within a reasonable commuting distance of their office location. Prospective candidates will learn more about their specific hybrid work schedule during their interview process. Hybrid work may not be permitted for certain roles, including, for example, certain FINRA-registered roles for which in-office attendance for the entire workweek is required.

SMBC provides reasonable accommodations during candidacy for applicants with disabilities consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please let us know at accommodations@smbcgroup.com.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor and triage alerts from security tooling across corporate and mission environments

  • Carry out vulnerability and exposure checks, and coordinate remediation with system owners

Minimum Qualifications

  • Equivalent internship, lab, or academic project experience will be considered
  • Experience monitoring and responding to security events on Windows, macOS, and Linux
  • endpoints

  • Proficiency in scripting and automation with PowerShell, Bash, or Python

  • (IDS/IPS)

This position is based in the Firm's global operations center in Tampa, FL or Dallas, TX.

General Description

The IT Security Analyst will assist in monitoring, analyzing, and responding to cyber security threats against Holland & Knight.

Key Responsibilities And Essential Job Functions

  • Assists with monitoring, analyzing, and responding to security events from a wide range of devices within the environment.
  • Ability to understand, prioritize and complete tasks by working independently or with a team.
  • Performs general operations maintenance support on security tools and agents.
  • Ability to process and correlate highly technical information from multiple sources in support of investigations.
  • Stays up to date with trends and current countermeasures for cyber security vulnerabilities, exploits, and other malicious activities.
  • Provides periodic “on-call” support of security operations during non-business hours.
  • Assists with the scanning of systems for known vulnerabilities and provide support in the remediation of any vulnerabilities found.
  • Analyzes and responds to previously undisclosed software and hardware vulnerabilities.
  • Identifies areas of risk to the Firm and assists with efforts to mitigate those risks to an acceptable level.
  • Maintains knowledge of vendor products, services and security technologies and recommends/implements their use.
  • Approaches all problems, projects, and incidents with a high level of professionalism, objectivity and an open mind to new ideas and solutions.
  • Expected to maintain a regular and predictable work schedule and full attention to and engagement in work activities on behalf of the firm during business hours unless otherwise approved or required by applicable law.
  • Special projects and additional duties as assigned.

Required Skills

  • Knowledge or ability to learn Microsoft Office Suite, or Microsoft 365.
  • Operating Systems: Windows Server, Active Directory, Linux, Windows 10/11
  • Network Technologies: Cisco LAN/WAN, VPN, DNS, DHCP
  • Security Infrastructure Applications: Endpoint Detection and Response tools, automated systems management, vulnerability management tools, password management tools, email server security.
  • Software: office productivity software, popular browsers, security related software analysis and protection, other business applications (accounting, practice management, CRM, etc.)

Required Qualifications & Education

  • Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university.

Preferred Qualifications & Education

  • 4+ years of experience in a technical support role or job-related experience, supporting security related technology in a diverse technology environment.
  • Experience with System Information and Event Management (SIEM) or other scalable log management solution, including the configuration and tuning of the system.
  • Experience with vulnerability scanning and reporting (e.g., Nessus, Qualys, Rapid 7, etc.)
  • Experience in monitoring and administrating various technical security controls such as firewalls, web filters and anti-virus solutions.
  • Current SANS and/or other security certifications preferred.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods of time.
  • Moderate or advanced keyboard usage.

Below are the benefits we offer: comprehensive medical (PPO and HDHPs), dental and vision plans including coverage for domestic partners; life and AD&D insurance; short and long term disability insurance; tax-advantaged accounts for health care expenses, including FSAs and HSAs; FSAs for dependent care; health advocacy services; behavioral health and counseling resources for all family members; 401(k); profit sharing; backup dependent care; senior care planning support; resources for individuals with development disabilities and their caregivers; and paid holidays and other paid time off, including paid leave for new parents.

descriptionHtml:
The Information Security Analyst II is a mid-level security professional responsible for monitoring, investigating, and responding to routine and moderately complex cybersecurity events across DBM Global. The role protects company systems and data by operating security technologies, coordinating incident containment and remediation, assessing security risk, and supporting compliance activities, including IT general controls for Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX).

This position works independently within established procedures, exercises sound judgment when evidence is incomplete, escalates high-impact or complex matters promptly, and helps improve detection, response, and preventive controls. The analyst also provides practical guidance to Level I analysts and partners with Infrastructure, Applications, and business teams to reduce risk.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor security alerts across networks, endpoints, identities, email, cloud services, and applications; distinguish actionable threats from benign activity.
  • Independently investigate routine and moderately complex incidents; determine scope, business impact, likely cause, and required response actions.
  • Coordinate containment, recovery, and remediation with technical teams and service providers; escalate significant incidents in accordance with the incident response plan.
  • Maintain incident records documenting evidence, findings, decisions, response actions, and remediation recommendations.
  • Operate security technologies, including SIEM, EDR, email security, identity security, network security, and vulnerability management tools.
  • Identify recurring alerts, false positives, and detection gaps; improve security controls, automation, procedures, and playbooks.
  • Perform vulnerability reviews and security assessments; track findings and coordinate remediation to closure.
  • Support security audits and SOX IT general control testing, including evidence collection, privileged-activity reviews, and corrective actions.
  • Help maintain security policies, metrics, and management reporting; stay current on relevant threats and vulnerabilities.
  • Provide technical guidance and case support to Level I Security Analysts.

Measures of Success

  • Security alerts and incidents are triaged, investigated, documented, and escalated within established service levels.
  • Incident records and audit evidence are accurate, complete, and usable by technical, compliance, and management stakeholders.
  • Assigned vulnerabilities, audit findings, and third-party risks are tracked transparently and remediated within agreed timelines.
  • Detection quality and response efficiency improve through measurable reductions in avoidable noise, repeat issues, and process gaps.
  • Cross-functional partners receive clear, actionable guidance and Level I analysts demonstrate improved consistency and capability.

Qualifications

 Experience & Education

  • Three to five years of progressively responsible experience in information security, cybersecurity, security operations, infrastructure security, or a related technical field.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, information systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated experience investigating security alerts and incidents and coordinating response with technical teams.

Technical Knowledge

  • Working knowledge of SIEM, endpoint security/EDR, email security, identity and access management, network security, vulnerability management, and incident response.
  • Ability to interpret security logs, correlate evidence across multiple sources, assess impact, and form defensible conclusions with incomplete information.
  • Understanding of common attack techniques, security control concepts, investigation methods, and remediation practices.
  • Familiarity with security and control frameworks such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST 800-53, CIS Controls, or equivalent, and with audit/compliance evidence practices.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Windows 11 and Microsoft 365 applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and Outlook.

Certification

  • Current ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) certification, or ability to obtain it within six months of hire or promotion into the role.
  • An intermediate certification such as CompTIA Security+, CySA+, ISC2 SSCP, a Microsoft security certification, or an equivalent credential is preferred.

Core Capabilities

  • Integrity and discretion — handles sensitive information responsibly, communicates candidly, and earns trust.
  • Analytical problem-solving — applies disciplined reasoning, tests assumptions, and looks beyond the first explanation.
  • Judgment and prioritization — makes timely, risk-based decisions and recognizes when escalation is required.
  • Communication and collaboration — translates technical findings into clear business impact and works effectively across teams.
  • Process discipline — follows established controls, maintains high-quality records, and improves repeatable workflows.
  • Learning agility and resilience — stays current, adapts to changing threats and technologies, and persists through complex investigations.

Equal Employment Opportunity

DBM Global is an Equal Opportunity Employer and maintains an Affirmative Action Program where required by applicable law. Employment decisions are made without unlawful discrimination.

descriptionHtml:
Our Deloitte Cyber team understands the unique challenges and opportunities businesses face in cybersecurity. Join our team to deliver powerful solutions to help our clients navigate the ever-changing threat landscape. Through powerful solutions and managed services that simplify complexity, we enable our clients to operate with resilience, grow with confidence, and proactively manage to secure success.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/31/2026.

Work you'll do

As a Managed Services Engineer III on the Cyber Operate Offering team, you will be responsible for...

  • Conduct advanced analysis of the results of monitoring solutions, assess escalated outputs and alerts from Level 1 Analysts, and ensure that all identified events are promptly validated and thoroughly investigated.
  • Perform root cause analysis and ad hoc searches related to relevant threat intelligence or emerging threats; assist the Threat Hunting team with advanced investigations as needed; and perform continuous monitoring of new threat sources and intel.
  • Analyze network data (e.g., packets and logs) and endpoint data (e.g., logs and malicious artifacts) using SIEM and various tools; analyze malware (executables, scripts, and documents) to determine indicators of compromise; and create signatures for future detection of similar samples.
  • Advise on development of detection engineering content and testing; provide guidance on response action plans for information risk events and incidents based on incident type and severity; and provide end-to-end event analysis, incident detection, and escalations to Shift Lead/Engineering/SDMs and SOC Manager using documented procedures.
  • When necessary, and with the SOC Manager's approval, devise and document new procedures and runbooks/playbooks; comply with and update processes, runbooks, templates, and procedures based on experience and best practice; track and report SOC SLAs; maintain individual certifications and learning requirements; and assist Shift Leads and fulfill Shift Lead responsibilities in their absence.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The team

Our Cyber Operate offering Operates clients' critical cyber assets as a fully managed service or working in partnership with clients. Provides talent, leading technologies, and processes to operate client cyber capabilities, including the identity lifecycle, security operations, threat intelligence, application security business transformation, and continuous compliance.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree, preferably in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Engineering, or related IT discipline; or equivalent experience
  • 2+ years of experience in cybersecurity or security operations
  • Experience in security technologies such as: Security information and event management (SIEM), IDS/IPS, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Proxy, Web Application Firewall (WAF), Endpoint detection and response (EDR), Anti-Virus, Sandboxing, network- and host-based firewalls, Threat Intelligence, Penetration Testing, etc.
  • Knowledge of Advanced Persistent Threats (APT) tactics, techniques, and procedures; understanding of possible attack activities such as network probing/scanning, DDOS, malicious code activity, etc.
  • Understanding of networking protocols such as TCP/IP, DNS, and HTTP; knowledge in system security architecture and security solutions
  • Ability to travel 10%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Work shifts on a rotating basis for 24/7 support of clients and work 50% of time from a Deloitte office.
  • Limited immigration sponsorship may be available.

At Zelis, we Get Stuff Done. So, let’s get to it!

A Little About Us

Zelis is modernizing the healthcare financial experience across payers, providers, and healthcare consumers. We serve more than 750 payers, including the top five national health plans, regional health plans, TPAs and millions of healthcare providers and consumers across our platform of solutions. Zelis sees across the system to identify, optimize, and solve problems holistically with technology built by healthcare experts – driving real, measurable results for clients.

At Zelis, AI is woven into the fabric of how we work. Every associate is expected - and empowered - to partner with AI to challenge the status quo, accelerate innovation, and amplify their impact. This is a place for builders with a growth mindset who act with agility, embrace change, and use modern technology to shape smarter solutions, exceptional experiences, and the future of our industry for our clients, customers, and our culture.

A Little About You

You bring a unique blend of personality and professional expertise to your work, inspiring others with your passion and dedication. Your career is a testament to your diverse experiences, community involvement, and the valuable lessons you've learned along the way. You are more than just your resume; you are a reflection of your achievements, the knowledge you've gained, and the personal interests that shape who you are.

Position Overview

Manages security operations tasks independently and contributes to the design and implementation of security controls.

As a Senior Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst, you’ll take the lead on investigating and mitigating security incidents across the organization. You’ll dig into digital evidence, guide teammates through complex problems, and help strengthen our overall detection and response capabilities. In this role, you’ll handle hands-on technical work like forensics and incident analysis, while also supporting the team by sharing knowledge, improving processes, and helping shape how we respond to threats. A component of this role will be focused around DLP and insider risk initiatives, which include incident analysis and process building in this space

Key Responsibilities

  • Incident Analysis & Handling: Triage alerts, investigate suspicious activity, lead incident response steps, and coordinate containment and recovery efforts.
  • Data Collection & Normalization: Make sure logs and security data are gathered correctly, cleaned up, and organized so the team can analyze them effectively.
  • Digital Forensics: Examine systems, files, logs, and network data to understand what happened during security events.
  • Mentoring & Training: Help newer analysts grow by sharing your experience, offering guidance, and running training sessions when needed.
  • Technical / Process Guidance: Assist team members with technical questions, tool usage, investigation methods, and established response workflows.
  • Shift Leadership: Act as the point person during your shift: manage workload, oversee investigations, ensure smooth handoffs, and support teammates. Participate in a rotating on-call schedule as required.
  • Innovation: Look for opportunities to improve processes, recommend new tools or automations, and help refine how the team operates.

Here is What You Can Expect on a Typical Day:

  • Reviewing alerts and logs to identify potential threats or unusual activity.
  • Leading or assisting with active investigations and driving them toward containment and resolution.
  • Running forensic analysis on hosts, cloud workloads, or network artifacts to uncover root causes and timelines.
  • Collaborating with IT, cloud, engineering, or other security teams to gather data or take action on investigations.
  • Sharing insights with teammates, helping them troubleshoot difficult cases, or walking them through an investigation technique.
  • Updating documentation, writing reports, or summarizing incident findings.
  • Teaching something new to the team—maybe a tool trick, a technique, or a better approach to analysis.
  • Handling shift responsibilities like queue management, monitoring ongoing investigations, and tracking priorities.
  • Identifying process gaps or tools that could be improved and proposing better ways to do things.
  • Perform other tasks required by management as needed

Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security, Information Technology, or 4+ years of equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years of enterprise level incident handling
  • Ability to partner with enterprise teams within a cybersecurity context, leveraging diverse ideas, experiences, thoughts, and perspectives to improve the organization.
  • Effective oral and written communication skills with experience in cybersecurity technical process documentation.
  • Demonstrated cyber defense and information security passion, including commitment to maintaining technical proficiency
  • Proven record of thought leadership via innovation and non-traditional solutions
  • Fundamental understanding of IT Security practices/programs/tooling, with demonstrated examples of driving initiatives forwards.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced cybersecurity certifications (e.g., GCFA, GCIA, GNFA, GCTI, GREM, GCIH, GCFA, GPEN, OSCP, etc.)
  • Cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.) certifications
  • Proficiency in scripting and high-level programming languages (Python, PowerShell, bash, etc.)
  • Functional knowledge of SIEM, SOAR, malware sandboxing solutions and related tools

Please note at this time we are unable to proceed with candidates who require visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Location and Workplace Flexibility

Zelis is headquartered in the U.S., with multiple locations across the country and in Hyderabad, India. Check out our locations to learn more about our offices. All employee work locations are based on the needs of the position and are determined by the Leadership team. In-office work and activities vary based on work and team objectives in accordance with Company policies.

While location expectations vary by role, candidates within approximately 50 miles of a U.S. office are generally preferred to support collaboration when needed. Our hybrid approach is flexible, and in-office presence is guided by team and business needs rather than a fixed weekly schedule.

Base Salary Range

$112,000.00 - $154,000.00

At Zelis we are committed to providing fair and equitable compensation packages. The base salary range allows us to make an offer that considers multiple individualized factors, including experience, education, qualifications, as well as job-related and industry-related knowledge and skills, etc. Base pay is just one part of our Total Rewards package, which may also include discretionary bonus plans, commissions, or other incentives depending on the role.

Zelis’ full-time associates are eligible for a highly competitive benefits package as well, which demonstrates our commitment to our employees’ health, well-being, and financial protection. The US-based benefits include a 401k plan with employer match, flexible paid time off, holidays, parental leaves, life and disability insurance, and health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Zelis is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

As a Senior Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst, you’ll take the lead on investigating and mitigating security incidents across the organization. You’ll dig into digital evidence, guide teammates through complex problems, and help strengthen our overall detection and response capabilities. In this role, you’ll handle hands-on technical work like forensics and incident analysis, while also supporting the team by sharing knowledge, improving processes, and helping shape how we respond to threats. A component of this role will be focused around DLP and insider risk initiatives, which include incident analysis and process building in this space

Key Responsibilities



- Incident Analysis & Handling: Triage alerts, investigate suspicious activity, lead incident response steps, and coordinate containment and recovery efforts.
- Data Collection & Normalization: Make sure logs and security data are gathered correctly, cleaned up, and organized so the team can analyze them effectively.
- Digital Forensics: Examine systems, files, logs, and network data to understand what happened during security events.
- Mentoring & Training: Help newer analysts grow by sharing your experience, offering guidance, and running training sessions when needed.
- Technical / Process Guidance: Assist team members with technical questions, tool usage, investigation methods, and established response workflows.
- Shift Leadership: Act as the point person during your shift: manage workload, oversee investigations, ensure smooth handoffs, and support teammates. Participate in a rotating on-call schedule as required.
- Innovation: Look for opportunities to improve processes, recommend new tools or automations, and help refine how the team operates.

- Reviewing alerts and logs to identify potential threats or unusual activity.
- Leading or assisting with active investigations and driving them toward containment and resolution.
- Running forensic analysis on hosts, cloud workloads, or network artifacts to uncover root causes and timelines.
- Collaborating with IT, cloud, engineering, or other security teams to gather data or take action on investigations.
- Sharing insights with teammates, helping them troubleshoot difficult cases, or walking them through an investigation technique.
- Updating documentation, writing reports, or summarizing incident findings.
- Teaching something new to the team—maybe a tool trick, a technique, or a better approach to analysis.
- Handling shift responsibilities like queue management, monitoring ongoing investigations, and tracking priorities.
- Identifying process gaps or tools that could be improved and proposing better ways to do things.
- Perform other tasks required by management as needed

- 3+ years of enterprise level incident handling
- Ability to partner with enterprise teams within a cybersecurity context, leveraging diverse ideas, experiences, thoughts, and perspectives to improve the organization.
- Effective oral and written communication skills with experience in cybersecurity technical process documentation.
- Demonstrated cyber defense and information security passion, including commitment to maintaining technical proficiency
- Proven record of thought leadership via innovation and non-traditional solutions
- Fundamental understanding of IT Security practices/programs/tooling, with demonstrated examples of driving initiatives forwards.

- Advanced cybersecurity certifications (e.g., GCFA, GCIA, GNFA, GCTI, GREM, GCIH, GCFA, GPEN, OSCP, etc.)
- Cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.) certifications
- Proficiency in scripting and high-level programming languages (Python, PowerShell, bash, etc.)
- Functional knowledge of SIEM, SOAR, malware sandboxing solutions and related tools

Company Description

Trupanion is a leading provider of medical insurance for cats and dogs in North America. Our mission is to help loving, responsible pet owners budget and care for their pets. At Trupanion, we offer a collaborative, casual, and pet-friendly environment where everyone is encouraged to be themselves.

Job Description

The Cybersecurity Analyst supports day-to-day Security Operations and Incident Response by monitoring and investigating threats, coordinating incident response, conducting threat intelligence and threat hunting, managing operational vulnerability workflows, and maintaining accurate cases and security metrics. Security Engineering owns security-platform engineering and vulnerability-scanning platforms, while technology and application owners execute remediation.

This position is open to candidates in the Seattle, WA area. You will have a hybrid remote/in-office schedule where you will work from our casual, pet-friendly office at least 3 days a week.

Responsibilities

Security Monitoring & Incident Response

  • Monitor and triage alerts across identity, endpoint, email, network, cloud, application, vulnerability, and data-protection technologies.
  • Validate, enrich, classify, and prioritize security events and investigate phishing, account compromise, malware, ransomware, unauthorized access, data exposure, insider threat, and third-party events.
  • Execute approved containment actions within assigned permissions and coordinate infrastructure-level or production changes with Technology Operations.
  • Collect and preserve evidence, identify affected users, devices, accounts, systems, repositories, and data, and support eradication, recovery validation, heightened monitoring, and closure.

Threat Intelligence & Threat Hunting

  • Collect and evaluate intelligence from commercial, government, industry, open-source, MDR, vendor, and internal sources.
  • Analyze threat actors, campaigns, tactics, techniques, procedures, indicators, exploited vulnerabilities, and targeted technologies for relevance to Trupanion.
  • Create tactical and operational intelligence products and operationalize findings through investigations, detections, hunting queries, watchlists, blocking actions, phishing simulation scenarios, and runbook updates.
  • Conduct hypothesis-driven hunts across identity, endpoint, email, network, cloud, and application telemetry using MITRE ATT&CK and document scope, queries, evidence, findings, and follow-up actions.

Vulnerability Management Partnership

  • Validate vulnerability findings, assess risk and business exposure, prioritize remediation using threat intelligence and incident telemetry, identify indications of exploitation, and escalate urgent vulnerabilities.
  • Perform threat hunts against affected technologies and recommend temporary containment or monitoring when active exploitation or incident correlation is identified.
  • Partner with Security Engineering, which owns vulnerability-scanning platforms, integrations, technical configuration, and platform reliability.
  • Coordinate remediation assignments with technology and application owners, maintain the vulnerability ticket flow, track progress against defined service levels, report overdue exposure, and escalate ownership or delivery issues through the established governance process.
  • Maintain operational oversight of vulnerability validation, prioritization, ticketing, remediation follow-up, SLA reporting, and escalation; remediation execution remains with the technology or application owner responsible for the affected asset or service.

Automation, Forensics & Case Management

  • Develop and maintain approved automation workflows, scripts, and playbooks for alert enrichment, investigation, authorized response, and case consistency.
  • Preserve identity, endpoint, email, cloud, network, application, and audit-log evidence under approved forensic, legal-hold, integrity, and chain-of-custody procedures.
  • Maintain complete case records covering severity, affected assets, evidence, analysis, actions, decisions, communications, and closure rationale.
  • Validate incident containment and corrective actions through available telemetry, testing, or monitoring.

Breach, Identity, Third-Party & AI Investigations

  • Support breach investigations by identifying affected repositories, records, data types, individuals, business entities, and jurisdictions for Legal and Privacy review.
  • Investigate token theft, MFA changes, privilege escalation, malicious application consent, mailbox manipulation, and compromised user, privileged, service-principal, or workload identities.
  • Investigate third-party, supply-chain, and AI-related security notifications or suspected misuse and document potential Trupanion exposure.

Operating Model & Continuity

  • Execute alert triage, investigations, MDR service monitoring, threat-intelligence analysis, threat hunting, vulnerability validation and prioritization, remediation follow-up, security metrics and reporting, case documentation, and authorized security-tool actions.
  • Escalate architecture, complex integration, detection-platform design, routine vulnerability-management administration, and permanent engineering needs to Security Engineering.
  • Provide structured handovers of active alerts, incidents, intelligence, investigations, and urgent exploitation-driven vulnerability exposures across operating regions.
  • Provide technical evidence to Legal and Privacy and do not independently determine legal privilege, regulatory interpretation, or notification obligations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Digital Forensics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in cybersecurity operations, incident response, IT operations, system administration, network security, or a related area.
  • Experience investigating alerts using SIEM, EDR/XDR, identity, email, cloud, network, or vulnerability technologies.
  • Knowledge of common attacker techniques, phishing, malware, account compromise, privilege misuse, lateral movement, exfiltration, and vulnerability exploitation.
  • Demonstrated experience applying threat intelligence and incident telemetry to vulnerability prioritization and exploitation assessment.
  • Experience with security automation or scripting, digital-evidence handling, identity investigations, third-party incident analysis, and structured case management.

Skills

  • Experience with Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft 365, Azure, identity security, privileged access management, cloud security, and endpoint environments.
  • Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK and common detection, threat-hunting, and incident-response methodologies.
  • Understanding of vulnerability scanning and remediation workflows and the division of responsibility between vulnerability-program governance, threat-led escalation, and asset-owner remediation.
  • Knowledge of NIST CSF, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NYDFS cybersecurity requirements, or privacy and breach-response obligations.
  • Relevant certification such as Security+, CySA+, SC-200, GCIH, GCIA, or equivalent experience is preferred.

Additional Requirements

  • Ability to support defined US business-hour coverage and participate in an escalation or on-call rotation.
  • Availability to assist with high-severity incidents outside normal working hours when required.
  • Ability to handle confidential, legally sensitive, and security-restricted information appropriately.

Compensation

  • The base salary range for this position is $120,000 - $140,000 on a full-time schedule.
  • Along with base compensation, Trupanion employees are currently eligible for monthly bonuses.
  • We want all employees to be invested in Trupanion’s success, so we grant Restricted Stock Units to all new team members. Our new hire grants vest over 4 years.

Additional Information

Benefits and Perks:

  • Full medical, dental, and vision benefits at no cost to the employee
  • Four weeks of paid time off and 9 paid float holidays (you can decide which days are most important to you!)
  • Five-week sabbatical after five years of employment
  • Open, casual, pet-friendly, and fun office environment
  • Free medical health insurance for your pet (1 dog or cat)
  • Paid time off to volunteer at nonprofit organizations
  • Seattle Office Amenities: Free on-site gym, free dog walking services for office pets during business hours, free parking, and paid ORCA cards.

For more information about Trupanion, visit https://trupanion.com/about

Learn more about how Trupanion has revolutionized our industry and the reimbursement model: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vdWZ4KHiPTQ

Trupanion is an equal-opportunity employer and embraces diversity. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, abilities, perspectives, and skills.

We will ensure that individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodations.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

descriptionHtml:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

About The Role

McKesson is seeking a Senior Cybersecurity Analyst to strengthen enterprise security monitoring and incident response capabilities. In this role, you will monitor and investigate security activity, serve as a senior escalation point for complex events, and help determine when an event should be managed as a cybersecurity incident.

You will work with technical and business partners throughout investigation, containment, eradication, and recovery. You will also improve detection logic, response playbooks, and operational processes based on threat intelligence, investigation findings, and lessons learned.

This position is well suited for an experienced security operations professional who combines hands-on technical knowledge with sound judgment, structured problem-solving, and clear stakeholder communication. You will also help develop junior analysts through mentoring and knowledge sharing.

What You’ll Do

  • Monitor, detect, analyze, and triage security alerts and events across enterprise environments.
  • Serve as a senior escalation point for security events and help determine when a cybersecurity incident should be declared.
  • Support incident investigation, containment, eradication, recovery, root-cause analysis, and post-incident reporting.
  • Identify common attacker tools, tactics, and procedures using threat intelligence and the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
  • Improve SIEM and EDR detections, investigation playbooks, alert quality, and incident-response processes.
  • Conduct or support proactive threat-hunting and security analysis activities.
  • Contribute to post-incident reviews, operational reporting, security metrics, and continuous-improvement initiatives.
  • Mentor junior analysts and communicate security risks and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.


Basic Requirements

  • 6+ years of professional cybersecurity experience, including experience in security operations, threat detection, or incident response.
  • Hands-on experience using Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) technologies.
  • Working knowledge of the MITRE ATT&CK framework and the NIST incident-response lifecycle.
  • One or more relevant cybersecurity certifications, such as SANS GCIH, GCIA, CompTIA CySA+, or an equivalent credential.
  • Demonstrated ability to investigate security events, analyze incomplete or conflicting data, and develop defensible conclusions.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, documentation, and prioritization skills.
  • Ability to communicate security findings, risks, and recommended actions to technical and non-technical stakeholders.


Preferred Skills/Experience

  • Experience with digital forensics, threat hunting, malware analysis, or security automation and orchestration.
  • Familiarity with cloud security, cloud-native security monitoring, and identity and access security.
  • Experience developing or tuning SIEM correlation rules, EDR detections, alerts, dashboards, or response playbooks.
  • Knowledge of cyber threat intelligence and common attacker tools, tactics, techniques, and procedures.
  • Experience working in healthcare, pharmaceutical distribution, supply chain, or software environments.
  • Familiarity with scripting or automation using Python, PowerShell, APIs, or SOAR technologies.
  • Ability to rapidly learn, assess, and recommend new cybersecurity tools and technologies.
  • Experience mentoring analysts or sharing technical knowledge across a security operations team.


Travel, Work Environment, and Physical Requirements

The work arrangement, location expectations, on-call responsibilities, and travel requirements will be based on the needs of the position and hiring team. The role may require extended computer use and participation in incident-response activities outside standard business hours.

We are proud to offer a competitive compensation package at McKesson as part of our Total Rewards. This is determined by several factors, including performance, experience and skills, equity, regular job market evaluations, and geographical markets. The pay range shown below is aligned with McKesson's pay philosophy, and pay will always be compliant with any applicable regulations. In addition to base pay, other compensation, such as an annual bonus or long-term incentive opportunities may be offered. For more information regarding benefits at McKesson, please click here.

Our Base Pay Range for this position

$122,500 - $204,100

In light of these scams, please bear the following in mind:

McKesson Talent Advisors will never solicit money or credit card information in connection with a McKesson job application.

McKesson Talent Advisors do not communicate with candidates via online chatrooms or using email accounts such as Gmail or Hotmail. Note that McKesson does rely on a virtual assistant (Gia) for certain recruiting-related communications with candidates.

McKesson job postings are posted on our career site: careers.mckesson.com.

McKesson provides equal employment opportunities to applicants and employees, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, age, genetic information, or any other legally protected category. For additional information on McKesson’s full Equal Employment Opportunity policies, visit our Equal Employment Opportunity page.

McKesson is committed to being an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and offers opportunities to all job seekers including job seekers with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to assist with your job search or application for employment, please contact us by sending an email to (United States) Disability_Accommodation@McKesson.com or (Canada) Accessibility@mckesson.ca. Resumes or CVs submitted to this email box will not be accepted.

Job Title

Medior SOC Analyst

Job Description

Location Marietta, GA | Hybrid

Join Vanderlande’s Cyber Security team as a Medior Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst, helping protect our global IT environment from evolving cybersecurity threats. You’ll investigate escalated incidents, analyze security events, coordinate response activities, and help strengthen our overall security posture.

What You’ll Do

  • Investigate security incidents escalated by Tier 1 SOC analysts.
  • Monitor and analyze security alerts, logs, and events to identify suspicious activity and potential threats.
  • Assess incident severity, scope, and impact, and coordinate containment and remediation efforts.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and document incident findings.
  • Partner with IT, infrastructure, application, and security teams to resolve incidents and vulnerabilities.
  • Support threat hunting, vulnerability identification, and continuous improvement of security controls.
  • Develop and improve SOC processes, playbooks, and incident response procedures.
  • Stay current on emerging threats, attack techniques, and cybersecurity best practices.

Tools & Technologies

  • Microsoft Sentinel / SIEM
  • Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR)
  • IDS/IPS
  • Firewalls and endpoint security solutions
  • Attack Surface Management
  • Sandboxing and threat hunting tools

What You Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in Security Operations, Incident Response, Cybersecurity Analysis, or related security roles.
  • Strong knowledge of threat detection, incident response, security monitoring, and SOC processes.
  • Hands-on experience with SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, firewalls, antivirus, and other security monitoring tools.
  • Working knowledge of networking, Windows and/or Linux, common attack techniques, vulnerabilities, and remediation.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative, global environment.
  • Flexibility to support rotational shifts or adjusted working hours when required.

Preferred Certifications

Relevant cybersecurity certifications are a plus, including

  • CompTIA Security+ or CySA+
  • CEH
  • GIAC certifications such as GCIH or GCIA
  • Microsoft SC-200
  • Other certifications in security operations, incident response, threat detection, or vulnerability management

Why Vanderlande?

Vanderlande is a global leader in logistics process automation for airports, parcel services, and warehouse solutions. You’ll have the opportunity to tackle global cybersecurity challenges while working with talented professionals in an innovative, international environment.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary package
  • 3 weeks of annual leave, prorated from the start of the financial year, including
  • 7 sick days
  • 9 paid holidays
  • 1 paid floating holiday
  • Flexible and hybrid working model (preferably 3 days in the office) supporting work-life balance
  • Access to Vanderlande Academy and a wide range of learning and development programs
  • Comprehensive medical insurance coverage
  • Opportunities to participate in Vanderlande communities and employee initiatives
  • Exposure to global cybersecurity challenges and industry-leading automation environments, with opportunities to expand your expertise across security operations, incident response, and threat detection
  • A collaborative culture built around Every day better, We care, and Team play

Ready to Apply?

If you’re passionate about cybersecurity and want to help protect a complex global technology environment, we’d like to hear from you. Apply through our careers page with your resume and a brief summary of your interest.

Diversity & Inclusion

Vanderlande is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability status, or other characteristics protected by applicable law.

As a member of the Information Services Department, the Senior Analyst, Cybersecurity Operations & Response supports the execution and continuous improvement of the Firm’s Cybersecurity Operations & Response program. This role is responsible for assisting with security operations, incident response activities, and threat and vulnerability management initiatives to help protect the Firm’s systems, applications, and data from cyber threats.

Essential Functions

  • Support the day-to-day operation and execution of the Firm’s Cybersecurity Operations & Response program.
  • Assist with the administration and continuous improvement of the Firm’s threat and vulnerability management program.
  • Develop, maintain, and update associated playbooks, policies, standards, and procedural documentation.
  • Participate in cyber event response activities, including investigation, containment, remediation, and recovery efforts.
  • Serve as a primary resource for security operations monitoring and incident triage activities.
  • Perform threat and vulnerability assessments and assist with remediation efforts to ensure systems are protected from known and potential threats.
  • Monitor security tools and alerts to identify, analyze, and escalate potential security incidents.
  • Develop and distribute reporting and metrics related to security operations, incidents, vulnerabilities, and overall program effectiveness.
  • Collaborate with internal teams and third-party providers to support security initiatives and operational improvements.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation and be available to respond to cybersecurity incidents and operational issues outside of normal business hours, as needed.

Additional Functions

  • Additional duties as assigned.

Education

QUALIFICATIONS (EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES):

  • Bachelor’s degree in information security or an equivalent combination of work and education required.

Experience

  • Minimum of five years of information security experience required including some direct experience with security operations, incident response, and threat/vulnerability management.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Knowledge of information security principles, including security operations, incident response, and threat and vulnerability management.
  • Knowledge of NIST and MITRE ATT&CK frameworks.
  • Experience in developing, documenting, and maintaining security procedures including security response playbooks.
  • Experience in developing, managing, and executing a threat and vulnerability management program.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to enable effective security event and problem resolution.
  • Ability to work well under minimal supervision.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong customer/client focus, with the ability to manage expectations appropriately, provide a superior customer/client experience, and build long-term relationships.

Work Environment & Physical Demands

This job operates in a clerical, office setting. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines.

Physical Requirements

Sedentary work: Exertion of physical strength to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects up to 10 pounds. Work involves sitting most of the time. Walking and standing is often necessary in carrying out job duties.

Compensation & Benefits

The salary ranges for this position apply to the respective listed locations. The salary range reflects a variety of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to experience, education, licensure and/or certifications, geographic location, market demands and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for a position. Reasonable estimates of the current ranges for this position are:

Description

Leidos has a current opportunity for a Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst supporting the Pentagon Reservation under the DISA GSM-O II TN24 Penetration Handling, Incident, System Health (PHISH) Support Services II program. This position supports a 24/7 SOC mission and requires availability for rotating shifts, including weekends, holidays, and inclement-weather operations.

The Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst supports continuous monitoring, detection, analysis, escalation, mitigation, and response to cybersecurity events affecting customer networks, endpoints, servers, applications, cloud environments, and mission systems. The analyst uses security telemetry, threat intelligence, established analytic procedures, and operational tools to identify suspicious or malicious activity; investigate potential compromises; document findings; and coordinate response actions with senior analysts, incident responders, cyber engineers, system owners, and mission partners.

This role is an experienced technical individual-contributor position. The SOC Analyst works independently to achieve day-to-day operational objectives and may own defined projects or technical processes within the SOC. The analyst contributes to operational cybersecurity, infrastructure support, and mission-support activities; collaborates with internal subject-matter experts to resolve technical problems; and may provide peer support, coaching, or technical review for less-experienced personnel.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Monitor, triage, and investigate alerts from Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools, intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS), authentication logs, NetFlow, packet capture, cloud-security tools, vulnerability data, and other available security sensors.
  • Analyze endpoint, host, network, identity, application, and cloud telemetry to identify anomalous, suspicious, or malicious activity.
  • Conduct assigned incident investigations by reviewing security logs and alerts, correlating evidence across available data sources, identifying potentially affected systems or accounts, assessing scope and potential impact, and escalating cases in accordance with established procedures.
  • Apply cyber threat intelligence and knowledge of adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) to validate alerts, identify indicators of compromise, prioritize investigations, and provide relevant context to incident responders and technical stakeholders.
  • Support approved containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident activities by collecting evidence, documenting actions, validating security controls, and coordinating with designated response personnel.
  • Perform computer forensic network and host analysis in support of incident investigations, threat-hunting activities, and evidence-based reporting.
  • Support proactive threat hunts, environment sweeps, and detection-validation activities based on known or emerging adversary activity, vulnerabilities, and organizational priorities.
  • Identify recurring false positives, control gaps, telemetry limitations, suspicious trends, vulnerabilities, and adversary behaviors; recommend improvements to detection logic, dashboards, analytic workflows, playbooks, and SOC processes.
  • Contribute to the development, testing, tuning, and documentation of detection use cases, correlation logic, analytic playbooks, standard operating procedures, work instructions, and knowledge-management artifacts.
  • Document analytic methods, evidence, findings, actions taken, escalation decisions, and recommended next steps in case-management and knowledge-management systems.
  • Prepare clear incident tickets, shift summaries, situational-awareness updates, and technical reports for SOC personnel, incident responders, system owners, and operational stakeholders.
  • Conduct authorized infrastructure-support activities, including device discovery, operating-system fingerprinting, service scanning, passive network scanning, and support to the configuration, testing, deployment, and maintenance of cybersecurity hardware and software.
  • Maintain proficiency with operational tools, cyber-defense methodologies, network and host analysis techniques, and evolving threats.
  • Support training, exercises, operational planning, and integrated cyber operations as assigned.
  • Collaborate with SOC operations, incident response, cyber engineering, threat intelligence, system administrators, and mission partners to share findings and support timely remediation.
  • Provide technical guidance, peer review, and knowledge sharing to junior analysts or other team members, as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Must have an active DoD Top Secret clearance with ability to obtain SCI
  • Must have DoD 8570 IAT II or higher certification (such as CompTIA Security+ CE, ISC2 SSCP, SANS GSEC, etc.) prior to starting.
  • Must be able to obtain DoD 8570 CSSP-Analyst certification (such as CEH, CySA+, GCIA, etc.) within 6 months of starting.
  • Bachelor’s degree in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, intelligence studies, or a related technical discipline, and 4-8 years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of relevant military service, cybersecurity education, certifications, and professional experience.
  • Experience supporting a SOC, CND organization, cyber protection team, incident-response team, network operations center, or comparable cybersecurity operations environment.
  • Experience monitoring and investigating cybersecurity events using SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, endpoint, network, identity, cloud, vulnerability, and log-data sources.
  • Working knowledge of incident-response processes, including alert triage, investigation, escalation, evidence collection, containment support, remediation coordination, and incident documentation.
  • Working knowledge of TCP/IP; common ports and protocols; network traffic flow; endpoint and operating-system fundamentals; authentication and identity activity; and enterprise security controls.
  • Familiarity with adversary TTPs, attack vectors, indicators of compromise, common malware behaviors, and analytic frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK and the Cyber Kill Chain.
  • Ability to analyze available data, identify gaps or uncertainties, apply established procedures, and communicate technically sound findings and recommendations.
  • Ability to prepare clear case notes, incident summaries, shift-turnover products, and technical reports for technical and operational audiences.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across SOC operations, incident response, cyber engineering, system administration, and customer or mission-partner organizations.
  • Ability to work independently on assigned operational objectives, technical processes, or projects, while recognizing when to seek assistance or escalate risk.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience using one or more enterprise SIEM platforms, such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, IBM QRadar, ArcSight, Elastic, or comparable tools.
  • Experience with EDR, antivirus, host-based security tools, IDS/IPS, network detection and response, vulnerability-management tools, NetFlow, or packet-capture analysis.
  • Familiarity with Windows and Unix/Linux operating systems, command-line tools, and system-administration concepts.
  • Experience with structured threat hunting, detection tuning, use-case development, or translating threat intelligence into analytic queries.
  • Familiarity with malicious-file triage, malware-analysis concepts, network-forensics techniques, or host-forensics artifacts.
  • Experience with scripting or automation using Python, PowerShell, Bash, or a similar language.
  • Relevant cybersecurity certification(s), including those required by the applicable contract, customer, or Department of War policy.

Senior Security Analyst - Managed Detection and Response

Our mission at Bitdefender is to reduce risk to customers’ business to allow them to achieve their objectives. We are focused on delivering real security value for an affordable price – no snake oil. To help in this mission, we are looking for a Senior Security Analyst. You will work in a tight knit, experienced team backed up by an international organization that’s been in business for 18 years.

Job Description

Ariens Company is seeking a motivated Cyber Security Analyst to join our team in Brillion, WI! In this role, you’ll play an important part in protecting our systems and information by supporting the day-to-day operations of our information security program. You’ll manage vulnerabilities through resolution, execute monthly patching, respond to escalated security alerts, administer security tools, support security awareness initiatives, conduct access reviews, and help ensure security controls are working effectively. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys problem-solving, cybersecurity, and making a meaningful impact on an organization’s security posture.

This position is located in Brillion, WI, and offers a hybrid work arrangement, with a minimum of three days per week onsite.

THE DAY TO DAY...

  • Triage and classify vulnerabilities identified across vulnerability management, attack surface, and threat intelligence feeds
  • Coordinate remediation with system owners and verify closure
  • Run vendor-provided assessment and evaluation tools to identify vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and control gaps.
  • Perform initial analysis of the results and route findings for remediation
  • Execute the monthly patch cycle for servers and workstations, investigate and resolve patch failures, and report on patch compliance
  • Perform first-line triage of security alerts escalated by the managed detection and response provider. Investigate and resolve routine incidents, and escalate confirmed or high-severity incidents to senior staff
  • Administer and maintain security software, including endpoint protection, email security, identity protection, and logging and monitoring tools
  • Apply configuration changes and tune detections under established standards
  • Run the security awareness program, including training assignment and completion tracking, phishing and social engineering simulations, and reporting of results
  • Perform email quarantine review and release, and investigate reported phishing and social engineering attempts
  • Conduct periodic user access reviews, verify offboarding and access revocation, and maintain the security exception and risk acceptance log
  • Gather information and produce control evidence across systems in support of audits, cyber insurance applications, customer security questionnaires, and other business requests
  • Apply and help enforce enterprise security policies, standards, procedures, and baselines, and recommend updates based on operational experience
  • Maintain current knowledge of information security practices, tools, frameworks, and attack and threat trends, and recommend practical improvements
  • Create and maintain security incident reports, runbooks, and operational documentation
  • Provide rotating on-call support and contribute to root cause analysis
  • Other duties as assigned

The Qualifications...

  • Degree in Information Security, Cybersecurity, Information Assurance, Computer Science, Information Systems, Computer or Network Engineering, Information Technology, or a closely related technical field is preferred
  • Minimum of 3 years of hands-on experience in information technology, with at least 2 years in a security operations capacity
  • Experience in vulnerability management, patch management, or security alert triage and incident handling
  • System and application administration experience in a Microsoft environment, including Active Directory and Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Defender, and Intune
  • Working knowledge of a scripting language for automation and reporting; PowerShell or Python preferred
  • Working knowledge of a recognized security control framework such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework or the CIS Critical Security Controls
  • Demonstrated organization, documentation, and written communication skills, including the ability to explain security requirements to non-technical staff
  • Experience in a manufacturing environment, including exposure to operational technology (OT) and non-IT-managed assets preferred
  • Ability to work independently on recurring responsibilities and to recognize when to escalate

Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without requiring sponsorship now or in the future.

360 SOC, headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, is a U.S.-based cybersecurity firm specializing in Managed Detection and Response (MDR) and Security Operations Center as a Service (SOCaaS). Established in 2015, the company offers a range of services designed to help organizations efficiently manage security challenges.

**Key Services Offered by 360 SOC:**

**Managed Detection and Response (MDR):** Combines advanced technology with expert human analysis to continuously monitor networks and endpoints for malicious activity, providing comprehensive threat detection and response capabilities. 

**Security Information & Event Management (SIEM):** Aggregates and analyzes activity from various resources across the IT infrastructure to identify potential security threats.

**Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR):** Streamlines incident response by automating workflows, integrating security tools, and orchestrating threat remediation processes, enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of the SOC.

**User and Entity Behavioral Analytics (UEBA):** Monitors user activities, behaviors, and patterns to detect insider threats and compromised accounts.

- **Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR):** Provides continuous monitoring and response to advanced threats on endpoints.

**Network Detection & Response (NDR):** Focuses on detecting and responding to threats within the network traffic. 

**Mobile App Support:** Offers clients a mobile application for real-time access to security alerts, incident management dashboards, and reports, ensuring constant connectivity and situational awareness.

The company has received industry recognition, including being named to MSSP Alert’s 2024 list of Top 250 Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs).

Additionally, 360 SOC has demonstrated its commitment to information security by successfully completing the System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2 Type II examination, ensuring the highest level of security by a 3PV.

  • Assist in vulnerability assessments and recommend remediation strategies.

Primary Objective

The Cybersecurity Analyst is an early-career, hands-on member of the CEENTA Information Technology team responsible for supporting daily cybersecurity operations, security monitoring, incident triage, documentation, risk and compliance activities, and end-user security support. The role works under the direction of the Cybersecurity Engineer and supports protection of CEENTA’s information assets, clinical and business systems, Microsoft 365 environment, endpoints, network infrastructure, applications, and sensitive data, including electronic protected health information (ePHI). The Analyst follows established policies, runbooks, and documented procedures; maintains accurate records of findings and actions; collaborates with IT and business stakeholders; and escalates complex, high-risk, or policy-level decisions to the Cybersecurity Engineer or IT leadership.

Essential Functions

Daily Security Operations, Monitoring, and Response (approximately 65% to 70% of role)

  • Monitor, triage, and document alerts from SIEM, EDR/XDR, email security, identity, endpoint, cloud, and web filtering platforms in accordance with documented procedures.
  • Perform initial investigation of reported phishing, suspicious user activity, endpoint alerts, unusual authentication activity, malware indicators, and other security events.
  • Escalate confirmed, complex, or high-risk incidents to the Cybersecurity Engineer with clear evidence, timelines, impact notes, and recommended next steps.
  • Administer day-to-day security platform activities such as email quarantine review, allow/block list requests, sender/recipient policy exceptions, web filtering exceptions, MFA support, EDR health checks, and security queue management.
  • Assist with Microsoft security and identity operations, including Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Defender, Conditional Access support, audit log review, and related security control validation as assigned.
  • Execute or support vulnerability scans, create remediation tickets, track ownership and due dates, validate remediation, and escalate overdue or high-risk findings.
  • Coordinate with Help Desk, Infrastructure, Network, Application, and vendor teams on security-related tickets, endpoint remediation, access questions, change activities, and incident follow-up.
  • Maintain accurate case notes, incident records, metrics, SOPs, runbooks, and knowledge base articles to support audit readiness, continuity, and repeatable operations.
  • Support tabletop exercises, incident response testing, phishing simulations, and operational improvement activities led by the Cybersecurity Engineer.

Risk, Compliance, Governance, and Program Support (approximately 30% to 35% of role)

  • Support HIPAA Security Rule, privacy, cyber insurance, internal audit, external audit, and other regulatory or contractual cybersecurity evidence requests.
  • Assist with vendor risk management intake, initial review, documentation collection, questionnaire review, SOC 2/HITRUST/BAA tracking, and summary reporting for Cybersecurity Engineer review.
  • Help maintain risk registers, exception logs, remediation trackers, policy inventories, security control documentation, and management reporting artifacts.
  • Assist with user access reviews, privileged access recertifications, control testing, and evidence organization in approved CEENTA repositories.
  • Support cybersecurity awareness activities, including phishing education, new-hire security orientation, newsletters, targeted end-user coaching, and security reminders.
  • Research emerging threats, vulnerabilities, healthcare cybersecurity risks, and best practices; summarize relevant findings for the Cybersecurity Engineer and IT leadership.
  • Participate in cybersecurity projects, technology implementations, change reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives as assigned.

Skills & Abilities

  • Foundational understanding of cybersecurity principles, including confidentiality, integrity, availability, least privilege, defense in depth, phishing, malware, social engineering, credential compromise, and common incident response concepts.
  • Working familiarity with Microsoft 365, Windows endpoints, Active Directory / Microsoft Entra ID, MFA, endpoint protection, email security, ticketing systems, and common enterprise IT operations.
  • Operational awareness of SIEM, EDR/XDR, email security, vulnerability management, web filtering, identity security, privileged access, and cloud security tooling.
  • Ability to follow documented procedures, analyze alerts and evidence, document findings clearly, and recognize when escalation is required.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain security issues to technical and non-technical audiences without unnecessary jargon.
  • Excellent attention to detail, sound judgment, discretion, and commitment to confidentiality when handling patient, employee, vendor, and business information.
  • Ability to manage multiple tickets, alerts, documentation requests, and deadlines in a fast-paced healthcare environment.
  • Customer-service mindset and ability to work collaboratively with clinical, administrative, technical, and vendor stakeholders.
  • Curiosity, coachability, and commitment to continuous development through hands-on learning, certifications, labs, and cybersecurity training.

Core Competencies

  • Analysis – Demonstrates the ability to review data, alerts, and evidence to reach sound, documented conclusions.
  • Cooperation – Recognizes that individual goals contribute toward accomplishing team outcomes and works effectively with the Cybersecurity Engineer and broader IT team.
  • Coordinating – Demonstrates the ability to circulate information, tickets, and follow-ups through the proper channels.
  • Dependability – Demonstrates the ability to follow through with work assignments and support management’s policies and procedures.
  • Learning Orientation – Actively seeks to expand cybersecurity knowledge, skills, and certifications, and applies new learning to daily work.
  • Relationships – Displays a professional, approachable, and compassionate attitude toward end users, colleagues, and vendors.
  • Integrity – Maintains the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information entrusted to the role.

Qualifications

Experience & Education:

  • One (1) to three (3) years of cybersecurity, information technology, help desk, system administration, network administration, healthcare IT, compliance, audit, or related technical experience is preferred.
  • Candidates with less direct work experience may be considered when they demonstrate equivalent preparation through internships, co-op programs, military experience, academic cybersecurity labs, capstone projects, security competitions, home labs, or relevant certifications.
  • Associate degree, bachelor’s degree, technical diploma, military training, or equivalent practical experience in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, healthcare technology, or a related discipline is preferred but not required when experience and aptitude are demonstrated.
  • Prior experience in healthcare, regulated environments, Microsoft 365 security operations, ticketing systems, vulnerability management, or security documentation is helpful.

Certifications & Licensure

One or more of the following certifications, or equivalent foundational credentials, is preferred but not required at the time of hire. If not held at hire, the employee is expected to work toward an approved foundational cybersecurity certification within the first twelve (12) months, based on manager direction and business need.

  • CompTIA Security+
  • ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
  • CompTIA Network+
  • CompTIA A+
  • Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity certifications (e.g., SC-900, SC-200)
  • Other equivalent foundational cybersecurity certifications

Advanced or management-level certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CISA, advanced GIAC credentials) are not required for this position.

  • Experience assessing Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) findings
