descriptionHtml:
FEDITC, LLC is a fast-growing business supporting DoD and other intelligence agencies worldwide. FEDITC develops mission critical national security systems throughout the world directly supporting the Warfighter, DoD Leadership, & the country. We are proud & honored to provide these services.

Overview of position:

We are looking for a CSSP Analyst, Senior provides advanced cybersecurity monitoring, threat analysis, and incident response support for DFAS networks. This position is responsible for identifying and responding to security threats, conducting threat hunting, managing endpoint security systems, and maintaining compliance with DoD cybersecurity requirements. The role also supports security audits, incident reporting, and operational readiness to ensure the protection of critical DFAS infrastructure.

A United States Citizenship and an active Top Secret DoD Security Clearance is required to be considered for this position.

Responsibilities

  • Provide senior-level 24/7 security monitoring, analysis, and incident response (ON-SITE REQUIRED)
  • Lead security event correlation and threat hunting activities
  • Monitor tools designed to protect DFAS networks from internal and external attacks (data exfiltration, malware, web attacks, unauthorized access)
  • Provide incident response, reporting (internal and external), and resolution on all CCE enclaves. 
  • Ensure 100% threat processing compliance for ESS management
  • Achieve 95% CMRS compliance for endpoint security
  • Support Command Cyber Readiness Inspection (CCRI) maintaining audit readiness state
  • Complete break/fix actions on schedule achieving 95% compliance
  • Complete assigned projects achieving 97% completion rate
  • Operate ESS, ACAS, ArcSight and incident response on network

Experience/Skills:

  • 8+ years cybersecurity/SOC analyst experience
  • CySA+ certification demonstrating advanced defensive analysis skills
  • DoD 8140 Cyber Defensive Analyst (Advanced) Playlist qualification
  • Expert-level SIEM analysis (Azure Sentinel, ArcSight, Splunk)
  • Experience with threat hunting and event correlation
  • Incident response and digital forensics experience
  • Knowledge of malware analysis and phishing investigation
  • Experience with ESS, ACAS, and network monitoring tools
  • Understanding of DFAS CSIRP incident reporting procedures

Preferred Qualifications:

  • GIAC certifications (GCIH, GCFA, GCIA)
  • Experience with DFAS CSSP SOC operations
  • Prior 24/7 SOC experience in DoD environment
  • Threat intelligence experience
  • Experience with Azure Sentinel KQL queries
  • Digital forensics certifications
  • Experience with classified network monitoring

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field

Certifications:

  • Cyber Defensive Analyst (Advanced) Playlist
  • CompTIA CySA+ or equivalent

Clearance:

  • Active Top-Secret clearance is required.
  • Must be a United States Citizen and pass a background check.
  • Maintain applicable security clearance(s) at the level required by the client and/or applicable certification(s) as requested by FEDITC and/or required by FEDITC’S Client(s)/Customer(s)/Prime contractor(s).

Who We Are

Williams International is a privately-owned company that develops and manufactures jet engines for both military and commercial aircraft applications. We are a company of creators who deliver pioneering ideas and technologies that lead the aerospace industry. Our culture fosters creativity, collaboration, and continuous learning to position our team members to inspire each other and provide quality products and supporting services that exceed the expectations of our customers.

The Opportunity

Williams International has an exciting opportunity for a SOC Analyst. The SOC Analyst will serve as our front-line defense against cyber threats. You will monitor our enterprise environment using advanced security tools, analyze real-time security alerts, and perform initial triaging to determine severity. Your primary goal is to ensure potential security incidents are identified, documented, and escalated or mitigated quickly to protect our infrastructure.

Responsibilities

  • Alert Monitoring: Continuously monitor Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) consoles, EDR platforms, and network dashboards for potential security incidents.
  • Triage & Classification: Perform initial analysis on high-volume alerts to filter out false positives and accurately categorize true security events.
  • Incident Escalation: Escalate validated threats to Tier 2/3 analysts or incident responders with clear, comprehensive technical documentation.
  • Log Analysis: Review and interpret logs from various sources—including firewalls, intrusion detection systems (IDS/IPS), active directory, endpoints, and cloud environments (AWS/Azure).
  • Phishing Investigations: Triage suspected employee phishing reports by analyzing email headers, attachments, and embedded URLs in a secure sandbox.
  • Ticketing & Documentation: Document all investigative steps, findings, and remediation actions within the designated ticketing system (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow).

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • SIEM/EDR Exposure: Minimum 1 year of hands-on experience navigating and querying SIEM platforms (e.g., Splunk, Elastic Search, Wazuh) and EDR/XDR agents (e.g., Defender for Endpoint).
  • Networking Foundations: Solid understanding of the OSI model, TCP/IP networking, common protocols (DNS, HTTP, SMTP, SSH), and basic network routing/switching.
  • Operating Systems: Proficiency in navigating and reviewing logs across Windows Active Directory environment and Linux environments.
  • Framework Familiarity: Basic knowledge of cyberattack methodologies, including the MITRE ATT&CK framework or the Cyber Kill Chain.
  • U.S. citizenship is required
  • Position requires the ability to obtain a U.S. Government Security Clearance, if needed. Candidates selected may be subject to a U.S. Government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. For more information on Security Clearances, please visit: U.S. Department of State.

Preferred Qualifications & Certifications

While not strictly required, the following credentials highly differentiate candidates:

  • Certifications: CompTIA Security+, CompTIA CySA+ (Cybersecurity Analyst), GiAC Security Essentials (GSEC), or Cisco Certified CyberOps Associate.
  • Scripting: Basic ability to read or modify scripts (Python, PowerShell, or Bash) to assist in automating repetitive daily workflows.
  • Home Labs / Capture the Flag (CTF): Active participation in hands-on learning platforms like TryHackMe, Hack The Box, or Blue Team Labs Online.

Additional Information

Williams International is a Drug Free Workplace where all new team members and contractors are subject to pre-employment drug testing for the following controlled substances: marijuana, cocaine, PCP, amphetamines, opioids and alcohol as policy dictates.

Job Posting Title:

Cybersecurity Analyst II




    • Hiring Department:

    Dell Medical School




    • Position Open To:

    All Applicants




    • Weekly Scheduled Hours:

    40




    • FLSA Status:

    Exempt from FLSA




    • Earliest Start Date:

    Immediately




    • Position Duration:

    Expected to Continue




    • Location:

    UT MAIN CAMPUS




    • Job Details:

    General Notes

    The Cybersecurity Analyst II is an intermediate level professional responsible for developing, maintaining, and enhancing enterprise cybersecurity programs that safeguard organizational systems, networks, and data. Reporting to the Manager of Enterprise IT Security and Operations, this role emphasizes program design, documentation, and continuous improvement in alignment with organizational standards. The position manages activities within one or more assigned cybersecurity domains such as risk management, incident response, vulnerability management, and threat intelligence, executed under established frameworks and with guidance, ensuring effective delivery of programs with moderate complexity. The Cybersecurity Analyst II updates policies, procedures, playbooks/runbooks, and automation to enhance efficiency and effectiveness. The role ensures alignment with regulatory frameworks such as HIPAA, FERPA, PCI DSS, GDPR, ISO 27001, and NIST and collaborates with IT and business teams to integrate security requirements into SDLC and operational processes. Additionally, the Cybersecurity Analyst II provides guidance to junior analysts and supports a risk-aware environment through outreach and education.

    Responsibilities

    Develops and Maintains Cybersecurity Programs

    • Designs and documents program components including policies, standard operating procedures, playbooks, and runbooks for one or more assigned cybersecurity domains such as risk management, incident response, vulnerability management, and threat intelligence, ensuring alignment with organizational standards and regulatory frameworks.
    • Implements automation and process improvements to enhance efficiency, strengthen domain controls, and support continuous improvement.
    • Maintains dashboards and performance metrics for assigned programs (e.g., SLA compliance, control health) and incorporates lessons learned into program updates.
    • Collaborates with IT and business stakeholders to integrate security requirements into operational processes and the software development lifecycle.
    • Coordinates with department IT teams, campus IT, and the Information Security Office (ISO) to review, implement, and monitor security controls on tools managed by campus IT and ISO (e.g., firewalls, DLP, MFA) to safeguard digital infrastructure.


    Executes Cybersecurity Operations

    • Manages investigations end-to-end and coordinates resolution for security events within scope.
    • Maintains and refines playbooks/runbooks; suggests workflow improvements based on lessons learned.
    • Implements automations for repetitive tasks (e.g., enrichment, triage, alerts, notifications).


    Supports Governance, Risk, and Compliance

    • Applies policies, standards, and procedures; performs control testing and gathers audit evidence.
    • Monitors adherence to HIPAA, FERPA, PCI DSS, GDPR, ISO 27001, and NIST frameworks.
    • Updates risk registers, proposes mitigations, and tracks remediation to closure.
    • Conducts third-party and vendor security assessments against organizational standards and documents follow-ups.
    • Helps facilitate awareness initiatives and tabletop exercises; offers coaching during activities.


    Reporting & Collaboration

    • Maintains dashboards and KPIs (e.g., MTTR, vulnerability SLA compliance, control health).
    • Prepares reports with actionable recommendations for stakeholders and leadership.
    • Partners with IT and project teams to embed security requirements in designs and changes; reviews changes for security impact.


    Marginal Or Periodic Functions

    • Maintains documentation specific to cybersecurity work (architecture diagrams, SOPs, inventories).
    • Represents the organization during audits and external assessments as assigned.
    • Participates in professional development and advanced training.
    • Supports disaster recovery and business continuity plan updates.
    • Adheres to internal controls and reporting structure.
    • Performs related duties as required.


    Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

    Problem Solving

    • Analyzes complex issues methodically and derives practical, evidence-based solutions.
    • Correlates multi-source telemetry to isolate root causes.
    • Tests alternatives and selects mitigations with minimal disruption.
    • Captures decision rationale and lessons learned.


    Decision Quality

    • Weighs risk, impact, and tradeoffs to make timely, sound decisions.
    • Prioritizes actions using clear severity/risk criteria.
    • Commits to reasonable containment steps under uncertainty.
    • Communicates next steps and contingencies.


    Functional/Technical Skills

    • Solid technical mastery across SIEM/SOAR, endpoint, vulnerability scanners, and core domains.
    • Enhances detections and enrichment workflows.
    • Executes investigations across OS/network/identity layers.

Seneca Technologies is hiring a Computer Network Defense Analyst. The Computer Network Defense (CND) Analyst supports a Department of War (DOW) agency contractor environment cybersecurity operations by monitoring, analyzing, and responding to network and security events across enterprise environments. The analyst plays a critical role in protecting information systems through continuous monitoring, threat detection, vulnerability assessment, incident analysis, and reporting. This position contributes to the agency's cyber defense posture by identifying risks, performing control gap analyses, supporting security operations center (SOC) activities, and driving continuous improvement of cybersecurity processes and monitoring strategies.

Important Information:

The following location and clearance qualifications are required for this role:

 

  • Location:  Mechanicsburg, PA. Employees will report onsite for the first 90 days after which the role becomes hybrid.
  • Clearance: Active Secret

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor security platforms, dashboards, and alerts to identify potential cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and suspicious activity.
  • Analyze security events and indicators of compromise; investigate and escalate incidents in accordance with established procedures.
  • Conduct control gap analyses to identify weaknesses in security controls and recommend mitigation strategies.
  • Support Security Operations Center (SOC) activities, including continuous monitoring and cyber defense operations.
  • Utilize vulnerability management and cloud security tools to assess and prioritize risks across enterprise systems.
  • Develop and maintain cybersecurity dashboards, metrics, reports, and operational status updates for leadership and stakeholders.
  • Review and correlate data from multiple security sources to identify trends, emerging threats, and areas requiring remediation.
  • Collaborate with system owners, network engineers, enterprise architects, and cybersecurity teams to improve overall security posture.
  • Assist with incident response activities, including triage, documentation, containment, and post-incident reporting.
  • Contribute to the development and refinement of continuous monitoring strategies, standard operating procedures, and cybersecurity best practices.
  • Support compliance, audit, and assessment activities related to Department of Defense cybersecurity requirements.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience in cybersecurity monitoring, threat detection, incident analysis, or Security Operations Center (SOC) environments.
  • Ability to analyze and interpret security events, logs, alerts, and vulnerability findings.
  • Experience performing control assessments and identifying security gaps within enterprise environments.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a mission-focused team.
  • S. citizenship and ability to obtain and maintain all required government security clearances, as applicable.
  • One or more of the following certifications:
    • CompTIA Security+ CE
    • CompTIA CySA+
    • GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH)
    • Splunk Core Certified User or equivalent Splunk certification
    • Comparable cybersecurity operations certification

Education and Experience

Possess current Secret Clearance plus one of the following:

Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related technical field with a minimum of four (4) years of experience in cybersecurity monitoring, cyber defense, incident response, or Security Operations Center (SOC) operations.

or Minimum of six (6) years of directly relevant cybersecurity, computer network defense, or SOC experience in lieu of a degree.

Technical Skills & Knowledge

Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)

  • Splunk
  • ArcSight
  • Comparable SIEM and log management platforms

Vulnerability and Security Monitoring Tools

  • Falcon CrowdStrike
  • Tenable Nessus
  • AWS Inspector
  • AWS GuardDuty
  • Enterprise network monitoring and security monitoring tools

Cybersecurity Knowledge Areas

  • Computer Network Defense (CND) operations
  • Security event monitoring and analysis
  • Threat detection and incident escalation
  • Vulnerability management
  • Network security principles and protocols
  • Continuous monitoring programs
  • Cybersecurity metrics and reporting
  • Security control assessments and gap analysis
  • Cloud security monitoring and AWS security services
  • Incident response processes and cyber defense best practices

Description

The Cybersecurity Analyst position is responsible for monitoring, analyzing, investigating, and responding to cybersecurity events across the enterprise. The role performs intermediate-level security operations, supports incident response and threat-hunting activities, improves detection quality, and partners with technology and business teams to reduce risk. The analyst independently handles routine and moderately complex investigations, documents findings, escalates significant issues, and contributes to the continuous improvement of security tools, processes, and operational readiness.

Here’s what you can expect from the job and what you need to be successful:

What You'll Do

  • Monitor and triage alerts from security technologies, including endpoint, identity, email, network, cloud, vulnerability-management, and SIEM platforms; validate severity, scope, and potential business impact.
  • Investigate suspected phishing, malware, compromised credentials, unauthorized access, data exposure, anomalous behavior, and other security events using available telemetry, threat intelligence, and documented procedures.
  • Execute incident-response procedures by containing threats within approved authority, preserving relevant evidence, documenting investigative timelines, and escalating high-severity or complex incidents to senior analysts and leadership.
  • Develop and perform threat hunts and detection validation activities based on emerging threats, vulnerabilities, indicators of compromise, adversary behaviors, and gaps identified through incidents or control reviews.
  • Tune security detections and alert workflows to improve fidelity, reduce unnecessary noise, document rationale and testing results, and ensure changes follow established review and change-management processes.
  • Create and maintain clear case records, dashboards, metrics, reports, runbooks, knowledge articles, and shift handoffs that support auditability, operational continuity, and leadership awareness.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure, network, cloud, identity, application, fraud, risk, and help-desk teams to coordinate remediation, validate recovery, and address recurring control weaknesses.
  • Participate in an on-call or after-hours response rotation as assigned, support security exercises and post-incident reviews, and share knowledge through peer mentoring and cross-training.

descriptionHtml:
Built on Trust. Driven by Protection.

DOT Security exists because businesses deserve a cybersecurity partner they can trust. As cyber threats became more sophisticated and disruptive, organizations needed more than technology; they needed experts who could help protect their people, operations, and livelihoods. Born from Impact Networking during a time when that need was rapidly growing, DOT Security was created to deliver a more proactive, personalized approach to cybersecurity.

What makes DOT special is that we've never lost sight of why we started. We exist to help organizations operate with confidence, while investing in talented people who are passionate about solving complex challenges and protecting what matters most. We've built something special, but we're far from finished. The people who join DOT today will help define what comes next.

Job Overview

As a Cybersecurity Analyst, you’ll be on the front lines of defense, working with a highly motivated team focused on analyzing, developing, and delivering solutions to stop adversaries. You’ll dig into alerts from defensive security systems and tools (such as IDS alerts, firewalls, and network logs) and decide whether each one represents a real threat.

This is an on-site position at our Security Operations Center in Mettawa, IL.

Responsibilities

Day to day, you will:

  • Monitor and analyze real-time alerts from our SIEM and other security tools to determine their cause.
  • Investigate network traffic, interpret logs, and analyze packet captures.
  • Detect, investigate, and alert on possible attacks, intrusions, anomalous activity, and misuse, while distinguishing real threats from benign activity.
  • Correlate information from sources across the enterprise to build situational awareness and gauge the effectiveness of an observed attack.
  • Investigate phishing emails.
  • Escalate events and incidents following established procedures and playbooks.
  • Document your findings and actions so they can be clearly shared with internal and external stakeholders.

As you grow with us, you’ll also have opportunities to:

  • Proactively hunt for threats and spot adversary activity that doesn’t trigger automated alerts.
  • Run intelligence-driven threat hunts to identify indicators of compromise (IOCs) and adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
  • Analyze intrusion sets to understand the weaknesses exploited, the methods used, and the impact on systems.
  • Hunt for phishing campaigns and emerging attack vectors.
  • Tune security tools for blocking, reporting, and proactive detection based on our customers’ business needs.
  • Contribute to projects that strengthen customer environments using lessons from incident response and threat hunting.
  • Develop and refine detection rules, automation playbooks, and security policies.

Qualifications & Experience

Skills and abilities:

  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain things clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Cybersecurity Knowledge

  • Knowledge of current threats and vulnerabilities.
  • Familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework (hands-on experience applying it is a plus).
  • Knowledge of authentication, authorization, and access control methods.
  • Understanding of defense-in-depth principles and network security architecture.
  • Understanding of IT security principles and methods, such as firewalls, demilitarized zones (DMZ), virtual private networks (VPN), and encryption.

Networking And Infrastructure

  • Understanding of network traffic flows, including Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) & Internet Protocol (IP), the Open System Interconnection (OSI) Model, and the IT Infrastructure Library (ITIL) framework.
  • Knowledge of network protocols such as TCP/IP, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP), Domain Name System (DNS), and directory services.
  • Knowledge of Windows/Unix ports and services.

Nice To Bring

  • Hands-on experience with Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms or log management systems.
  • Experience in an IT infrastructure role such as Systems Administrator, Network Administrator, Systems Engineer, or Network Engineer.
  • Ability to analyze malware.
  • Understanding of system and application security threats, such as buffer overflow, mobile code, cross-site scripting (XSS), PL/SQL injections, race conditions, covert channels, replay attacks, return-oriented attacks, and malicious code.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Information Technology, or Cybersecurity. Relevant work experience may be substituted for a degree.
  • Master’s degree or four years of relevant work experience is a plus.

Certifications

  • CompTIA Security+ or CompTIA CySA+ is preferred.
  • Also highly valued: TCM Security – PSAA (Practical SOC Analyst Associate), ECTHP (Certified Threat Hunting Professional), or BTL1 (Blue Team Level 1).

Compensation

Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skillset, experience and training, licensures and/or certifications, and other organizational needs.

DOT Security may offer applicable incentive compensation plans depending on role and/or department.

Full compensation details can and will be discussed with an Impact Talent Acquisition team member at the start of the interview process.

Benefits We Take Pride In

  • 5-year Tiffany & Co. Gift Card or Custom Menswear, 10-year Custom Rolex, 20-year $20,000 Check incentive rewards
  • Valuable time off with up to 20 days of PTO, 7 Paid Sick Days, 12+ paid holidays, and Paid Parental Leave
  • Development and growth opportunities with on-going training & continued education reimbursement
  • 401(K) & retirement plans with complimentary financial advisory services
  • Comprehensive health, disability, life, dental, and vision plans

Work Authorization & Immigration Sponsorship

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States at the time of application. Immigration sponsorship may be considered in select cases based on business need, cost, workforce planning, and applicable government requirements. Impact does not guarantee sponsorship for any visa category and may decline certain petitions based on associated costs or regulatory requirements.

Certain positions within DOT Security may involve access to information, technology, software, or technical data that is subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Where required by applicable law based on the nature of the role, individuals in such positions must qualify as a “U.S. Person,” as defined by law, or otherwise be eligible to obtain any required government authorizations.

Recruitment Communications Notice

Please Note: All recruiting operations for DOT Security are managed by the Impact Networking Talent Acquisition Team. As a result, candidates should expect recruitment-related communications including application updates, interview scheduling, requests for information, and offer discussions to come from members of the Impact Talent Acquisition team.

We appreciate your interest in DOT Security and look forward to getting to know you.

Compensation Range: $75K - $100K

Job Summary

The Cyber Security Fusion Center Analyst monitors, analyzes, correlates, and communicates cyber security events affecting the electric utility. The analyst focuses on cyber activity across enterprise information technology and operational technology environments, correlating it with related physical security and IT events to create a unified cyber operating picture. This role supports rapid detection, sound escalation, coordinated cyber incident response, and the reliable delivery of critical electric service.

Job Description

What you’ll do:

  • Maintain continuous cyber situational awareness by monitoring security platforms, IT and OT security dashboards, physical security notifications, and other relevant sources.
  • Triage and validate alerts; correlate IT and OT cyber events with related physical security and IT operational indicators to identify emerging threats, coordinated activity, and potential risks to utility operations.
  • Conduct initial analysis of suspicious activity across enterprise IT and operational technology environments and document findings, evidence, assumptions, and recommended actions.
  • Escalate incidents according to established severity levels, decision thresholds, notification procedures, and incident command processes.
  • Coordinate cyber event information sharing among cybersecurity, IT, OT, physical security, system operations, legal, communications, and executive stakeholders.
  • Produce timely incident notifications, situation reports, intelligence notes, shift briefings, dashboards, and executive summaries tailored to the audience.
  • Support incident response activities, including case creation, evidence preservation, timeline development, stakeholder notifications, task tracking, and transition to recovery.
  • Enrich alerts and investigations using threat intelligence, asset criticality, known vulnerabilities, system dependencies, and current operating conditions.
  • Track open actions and unresolved risks; maintain accurate logs and case records in accordance with retention and audit requirements.
  • Participate in exercises, after-action reviews, procedure updates, and continuous-improvement initiatives.
  • Develop and maintain playbooks, standard operating procedures, contact lists, escalation matrices, and knowledge articles.
  • Build trusted relationships with internal partners, peer utilities, industry groups, government partners, and law enforcement as authorized.



Preferred Requirements:

  • Experience in electric utility, critical infrastructure, energy, industrial control system, or operational technology sectors.
  • Familiarity with security information and event management, endpoint detection and response, threat intelligence, vulnerability management, network monitoring, OT network security monitoring, or physical security alerting platforms.
  • Knowledge of industrial control system concepts, OT cyber threats, utility operations, and how cyber events can intersect with physical security and IT incidents.
  • Experience producing executive briefings, incident reports, intelligence products, or common operating picture updates.
  • Relevant certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GCIH, GCIA, CISSP, or comparable credentials.



What We're Looking For:

Education requirements are listed below:

  • Bachelor's degree OR Associates degree with 2 years relevant experience in system administration/help desk/security (cyber or physical).
  • High School Diploma/GED with 4 years relevant experience in IT system administration/help desk/security (cyber or physical).
  • Graduation from an approved Cybersecurity Program; alternatively may have non-degree qualifications (such as hands-on demonstrated ability in a technical interview/assessment).



Work Experience requirement listed below:

  • 4 or more years of Information Technology related experience.
  • 2 or more years of security related experience, which may include military/government work experience in addition to any experience identified above.



What You’ll Get:

In addition to a competitive compensation, AEP offers a unique comprehensive benefits package that aims to support and enhance the overall well-being of our employees.

Where Putting the Customer First Powers Everything We Do!

At AEP, we’re more than just an energy company — we’re a team of dedicated professionals committed to delivering safe, reliable, and innovative energy solutions. Guided by our mission to put the customer first, we strive to exceed expectations by listening, responding, and continuously improving the way we serve our communities. If you're passionate about making a meaningful impact and being part of a forward-thinking organization, this is the company for you!

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience in security operations (SOC), incident response, threat hunting, IT compliance or equivalent.
  • Experience with log analysis, data querying (SQL), or monitoring security controls.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience coordinating cross-functional security incidents.
  • Familiarity with Google’s data analysis infrastructure (e.g., business intelligence platform).
  • Understanding of common security frameworks, access governance models, and the vulnerability management life-cycle.
  • Ability to translate operational security findings into technical engineering requirements.

About The Job

Google creates products and services that make the world a better place, and gTech’s role is to help bring them to life. Our solutions are rooted in our technical skill, product expertise, and a thorough understanding of our customers’ needs. Whether the answer is a bespoke solution to solve a unique problem, or a new tool that can scale across Google, everything we do aims to ensure customers benefit from the full potential of Google products.

gTech Risk helps protect Google and its users by identifying and implementing controls for risks. To ensure gTech's security and agility, the team analyzes gTech business processes to find control gaps, collaborates with stakeholders to resolve these gaps, and provides risk expertise to engineer innovative solutions.

gTech Risk Solutions Engineering is transforming from a manual process led organization to a proactive engineering powerhouse. Operating as a federated security partner to Google's central security organizations, we design and build highly contextualized security solutions tailored for the gTech business ecosystem. Our mission is upfront risk prevention through technical delivery excellence, shifting the paradigm from "risk-chasing" to "prevention by design."

In this role, you are the observability and feedback engine of the team. You will ensure our autonomous remediations and agentic workflows are operating securely and effectively. You will monitor the automated flows of agentic tooling and manage the operational fallback tiers when AI workflows flag anomalies. Utilizing your deep security domain knowledge, you will conduct threat hunting, perform complex log analysis (SQL/Business Intelligence Platform), and triage incident alerts. Crucially, your intelligence will feed directly back into our engineering roadmap.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $123000 - $176000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

  • Monitor agentic/automated flows, triage edge cases, and manage operational fallbacks when agentic workflows require human escalation.
  • Run day-to-day threat hunting operations, perform advanced log analysis (SQL/Business Intelligence Platform), and triage data transfer and access alerts.
  • Monitor access alerts, audit permission mappings, and verify the efficacy of our automated provisioning tools.
  • Act as triage lead for the gTech ecosystem: monitor incident queues, conduct initial forensic analysis, and orchestrate handoffs with central Detection and Response (D&R) teams.
  • Verify false positives, triage legacy issues, and track remediation velocity to ensure alignment with global service level objective timelines.

descriptionHtml:
Who is Fusion Technology?

Fusion Technology is a performance-driven HUBZone Small Business concern residing in the heart of the beautiful mountainsides of West Virginia, steps away from the Federal Bureau of Investigation's Criminal Justice Information Services Division's Headquarters. Founded in 2007 by an Engineer-by-trade, Fusion Technology dedicates our valuable resources to providing comprehensive IT services and solutions to mission-critical US Government programs and the Intel Community.

Position Location: Washington, DC

Who are you?

Security-cleared Professional: An active TS Clearance is required to be considered for this position.

Education and Experience: You have a Bachelor's Degree from an accredited college or university in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field.

  • 8+ years of experience in a cybersecurity-focused role.
  • Individuals must be capable of conducting in-depth technical analysis, confirming compliance information and maintaining a detailed record of all actions taken, evidence and communications.
  • Experience assessing information systems for compliance with Federal cybersecurity policies, standards, and technical security requirements, including NIST guidelines, encryption, multi-factor authentication, vulnerability management, and centralized logging.
  • Knowledge of vulnerability management processes, including identifying and analyzing system vulnerabilities, documenting security deficiencies, and developing remediation recommendations.
  • Proficiency in analyzing security logs, network traffic, and threat intelligence data to identify anomalous activity, potential data exfiltration, indicators of compromise, and emerging cybersecurity threats.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity audits, security assessments, incident response activities, and digital forensic investigations, including evidence preservation, technical reporting, and coordination with cybersecurity teams and stakeholders.

Preferred Certifications: CompTIA CySA+, CompTIA CASP+, CompTIA PenTest+, CompTIA SecurityX, EC-Council Certified Ethical Hacker (C|EH), EC-Council Certified Incident Handler (C|IH), GIAC GPEN, GIAC GCIH

What You'll Do

The Cybersecurity Analyst assists the Customer in researching and enforcing technical cybersecurity compliance of the Agency's systems. Investigates the detailed system attributes of encryption, vulnerability management, multi-factor authentication, and centralized logging and auditing, among other disciplines. The analyst should have detailed knowledge of the federal standards and technologies used to carry out the required disciplines and will provide technical summaries and input on the data. The Analyst works with the Security Assessment Teams (Red, Blue, Purple, as well as the DCISO/CISO) to perform detailed analysis and identify noncompliant systems and possible vulnerabilities and will assist in providing methods to remediating shortcomings to personnel and other stakeholders both internal and external for affected systems.

Other Responsibilities Include

  • Assisting in interpretation and implementation of Federal Government requirements for systems when necessary and coordinates various audits and data calls which are regularly carried out against system data.
  • Analyzing logs to determine anomalous traffic and potential exfiltrated data.
  • Maintaining working knowledge of current vulnerabilities of systems and how they can be exploited.
  • Interpreting guidance and technical requirements for implementation security requirements to prevent security breaches from happening and disseminates the guidance in a more readable format to others.
  • Ensuring that current Federal Government security policies are being followed to the extent they able to and all required documentation is provided.
  • Responding to incidents when required to assist in detection, isolation, remediation, and investigation of the incident.
  • Participating in After Action Reviews (AARs) of incident responses.
  • Understanding and analyzing threat intelligence data to identify emerging threats and proactively defend against them.
  • Assisting with vulnerability management notifications from OGAs, the Agency, and vendors to ensure that required vulnerabilities within identified systems are remedied within the required timeline and reported accurately within that timeline.
  • Produces, analyzes, and interprets forensically sound images of data and other electronic storage media when required or requested.

What Matters To You Matters To Us.

Fusion Technology values its employees and works hard to ensure proper care for them and their families. We desire to compensate employees in a competitive, motivational, fair, and equitable way with other employers in the marketplace. Salary is only one component of employee compensation but an integral part of recruiting and retaining qualified employees. However, at Fusion Technology, we take a comprehensive approach and consider each employee's needs to tailor a compensation plan that provides financial security and peace of mind. Our competitive package includes a best-in-class matching 401K program, a comprehensive healthcare plan through Cigna, a competitive employer contribution to a health savings account, vision and dental plans, life insurance, short- and long-term disability, and personal leave, in addition to paid certifications and training.

Fusion Technology LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We respect and seek to empower each individual and support the diverse cultures, perspectives, skills, and experiences within our workforce. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

Salary: $100000 - $120000 per year

descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

Job Summary

We are searching for an IT Security Analyst II to support and strengthen the security, monitoring, and compliance of our multi-site, hybrid corporate IT infrastructure, on-premises systems, and SaaS application platforms. This role will independently perform security monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response, policy and control administration, and compliance activities within established cybersecurity programs and procedures. The role will collaborate with IT infrastructure, application owners, business teams, and external service providers to identify, assess, and remediate cybersecurity risks. The ideal candidate will have hands-on cybersecurity operations experience in a medium- or enterprise-scale environment, preferably within a highly regulated industry or an organization subject to NIST 800-171, CMMC, or similar security frameworks.

Responsibilities

  • Independently monitor and analyze activity across computer networks, systems, cloud platforms, and SaaS applications for suspicious activity and potential security incidents.
  • Configure and onboard supported IT systems and appliances into the enterprise SIEM, including validating log collection and supporting detection and investigation capabilities.
  • Analyze, investigate, and respond to SIEM, endpoint protection, firewall, identity, and access management alerts, escalating complex or high-risk events as appropriate.
  • Investigate and document routine and moderately complex security incidents; coordinate containment and remediation activities and escalate as appropriate.
  • Perform vulnerability management activities, including scanning, analysis, prioritization, reporting, and remediation tracking through closure.
  • Work with IT infrastructure teams to identify, assess, prioritize, and resolve network, endpoint, cloud, and application security risks.
  • Apply and support the maintenance and enforcement of internal IT security policies and procedures, including data handling, acceptable use, access control, and incident response.
  • Perform assigned audit, compliance review, evidence collection, and control assessment activities against applicable regulatory frameworks.
  • Administer and monitor assigned security controls for firewalls, endpoint protection, encryption, identity and access management, multi-factor authentication, and secure remote access.
  • Review user access, permissions, and privileged accounts to enforce least-privilege and zero-trust principles.
  • Support security awareness initiatives and reinforce cybersecurity best practices across the organization.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of security incidents, risks, procedures, control evidence, and remediation activities.
  • Coordinate assigned security activities with third-party cybersecurity vendors and managed service providers.
  • Monitor developments in current cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, trends, and regulatory requirements.
  • Develop and maintain metrics and reports on security alerts, vulnerabilities, incident response, compliance status, and remediation progress.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education, certifications, training, and applicable work experience.
  • 4+ years of relevant work experience in IT security, cybersecurity operations, security operations, or a closely related technical security role.
  • Hands-on experience analyzing security events and alerts using SIEM platforms, endpoint detection and response tools, vulnerability scanners, firewalls, and ticketing systems.
  • Experience supporting identity, access, and endpoint security technologies, including Microsoft 365, Entra ID, SSO, MFA, endpoint management, or zero-trust initiatives.
  • Experience supporting vulnerability management, security incident response, or security control administration.
  • Familiarity with security frameworks such as NIST 800-171, CMMC, ISO 27001, or similar standards is preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GSEC, SSCP, or similar are preferred.
  • Prior work experience in a highly regulated industry, government contractor environment, engineering organization, industrial/manufacturing company, and/or energy company is preferred.
  • Prior work experience in a high-growth or rapidly scaling environment is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Working knowledge of networking principles, endpoint security, identity and access management, cloud services, and common cybersecurity controls.
  • Working knowledge of security incident response principles and processes, including investigation, escalation, containment, remediation, recovery, and documentation.
  • Ability to independently analyze routine and moderately complex security alerts and events, identify relevant patterns and indicators, and determine appropriate response or escalation.
  • Ability to assess cybersecurity risks and prioritize remediation activities based on severity, likelihood, business impact, asset criticality, and established organizational criteria.
  • Ability to analyze vulnerability findings, distinguish actionable risk from lower-priority findings, and coordinate remediation through closure.
  • Ability to develop and interpret cybersecurity metrics, reports, and trend data related to incidents, vulnerabilities, compliance, and remediation progress.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with IT infrastructure teams, application owners, business stakeholders, third-party vendors, and managed service providers to investigate security issues and implement corrective actions.
  • Ability to apply cybersecurity policies, standards, and control requirements in support of security operations, audits, compliance reviews, and control assessments.
  • Ability to administer and monitor assigned security technologies and controls within established configurations, standards, and procedures.
  • Ability to maintain accurate, complete, and audit-ready security documentation and control evidence.
  • Ability to manage multiple security priorities and assigned remediation activities in a changing operational environment.
  • Ability to analyze technical security problems and identify practical, risk-based solutions.
  • Ability to communicate cybersecurity risks, findings, and remediation requirements effectively to technical and non-technical audiences.

Physical Demands

  • Remaining in a stationary position, often standing, or sitting for prolonged periods
  • Communicating with others to exchange information

Environmental Conditions

  • General office environment
  • Noisy environments
  • Prototyping/Test Facilities
  • Manufacturing/Industrial Environments

Safety and PPE

  • Reading and interpreting hazardous warning signs
  • Reporting issues with equipment or unsafe conditions
  • Wearing proper PPE, to include face mask, face shields, gloves, safety shoes, or other PPE as required

Travel

  • Some travel may be required (5%)

Certification

  • Professional cybersecurity certifications such as CompTIA Security+, CySA+, ISC2 SSCP, GIAC GSEC, Microsoft security certifications, or similar is preferred but not required.

Additional Requirements

  • Occasionally requires working weekends
  • Occasionally requires extended hours to support launch and critical project timelines

The salary range for this position is $108,735 to $127,923 for employees working onsite at our Alameda, CA headquarters. The range provided in this job posting represents the typical range or starting rate of candidates hired in California. Factors that maybe used to determine your actual salary may include your education, experience, knowledge, skills, ability and the market data for your work location, and a comparison to other employees already in the role.

About Our Benefits

We know that we have some of the most talented and dedicated employees, and we believe in rewarding them accordingly. If you work here, full-time employees (excludes interns) expect to have access to the benefits below:

  • Competitive compensation packages
  • Medical, dental and vision benefits for employees and their dependents
  • Paid Vacation
  • 401(k) and pre-tax health insurance, dependent care, and commuter benefits (FSA)

Kairos Power is committed to building a diverse workforce that reflects the communities where we do business. Kairos Power is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. We actively welcome people of different experiences, abilities, and perspectives.

Kairos Power participates in E-Verify.

Candidates only, no recruiters or agencies please.

Note: You are applying for a position that is located in a facility that handles information that is subject to export control restrictions by the Department of Energy under 10 CFR Part 810. To work in this facility, you need to be authorized by the Department of Energy to access Part 810-controlled information. Foreign nationals who are citizens of countries that are not on the Department of Energy’s general authorization list (link below) are not permitted to work in our facility unless the Department of Energy issues an export control license to the company to permit that individual to have access to Part 810-controlled information. The following questions are intended to determine the licensing requirements that may apply. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/10/appendix-A_to_part_810

Summary:

We are seeking a talented and motivated Cyber Security Analyst to join our team. The ideal candidate will play a critical role in protecting our organization's digital assets and ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of our information systems. As a Cyber Security Analyst, you will be responsible for monitoring, analyzing, and responding to security threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents to maintain a secure and compliant environment.

Company Information:

National Heritage Academies (NHA) partners with communities to build and operate public charter schools. Founded in 1995, today NHA serves over 100 schools in nine states, with more than 65,000 students in kindergarten through 12th grade. Our schools are designed to eliminate the achievement gap and provide school choice to families so their children are prepared for success in college, career, and life. A majority of our schools consistently outperform their local district on the state test. According to the Center for Research on Education Outcomes at Stanford University, NHA is a leading performer among charter schools and management organizations, outperforming both conventional district schools and other charter school operators. In addition, according to our employee survey, over 90% of respondents agree that the work they do is meaningful to them. Join our team.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Monitor security alerts and events from various sources, including intrusion detection systems, SIEM tools, and log files.
  • Analyze security data to identify and investigate potential security incidents and threats.
  • Stay current with emerging threats and vulnerabilities to proactively identify potential risks.
  • Respond promptly to security incidents and breaches, following established incident response procedures.
  • Contain and mitigate security incidents to minimize impact and prevent further unauthorized access or data loss.
  • Document incident details and lessons learned for future improvement.
  • Perform regular vulnerability assessments and scans of the organization's infrastructure, applications, and systems.
  • Identify and prioritize vulnerabilities, and work with relevant teams to remediate them.
  • Keep software and systems up-to-date with patches and security updates.
  • Assist in the development and enforcement of information security policies, standards, and procedures.
  • Provide guidance and training to staff on security best practices and awareness.
  • Manage and configure security tools and technologies, such as firewalls, antivirus, intrusion detection/prevention systems, and encryption solutions.
  • Evaluate and recommend new security technologies to enhance the organization's security posture.
  • Generate and maintain reports related to security incidents, vulnerabilities, and compliance for management and regulatory purposes.
  • Maintain accurate records of security activities and documentation of security configurations and procedures.
  • Additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field. Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISA, CompTIA Security+) are a plus.
  • Proven experience in cyber security, with a minimum of 2-4 years in a similar role.
  • Strong understanding of security principles, practices, and technologies.
  • Proficiency in security tools and technologies, such as SIEM, IDS/IPS, antivirus, firewall, and vulnerability assessment tools.
  • Knowledge of regulatory requirements (e.g., FERPA, ISO 27001) and ability to ensure compliance.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to think critically and respond effectively to security incidents.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams and communicate security issues to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Continuous learning mindset to keep up with evolving cyber threats and security best practices.

This is an in-person position at our NHA Service Center located at 3850 Broadmoor Ave., Grand Rapids, MI.

Please click here to find out more about our core values.

National Heritage Academies is an equal-opportunity employer

descriptionHtml:
Overview

Titan Machinery is seeking a Security Analyst I to help safeguard our systems, data, and users from evolving cyber threats. In this role, you'll work closely with Information Security, Infrastructure, and Help Desk teams to monitor security events, investigate incidents, manage vulnerabilities, administer security controls, and support continuous improvement of our cybersecurity program. This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to grow their cybersecurity career while gaining hands-on experience with enterprise security tools, incident response, vulnerability management, and identity security.

Responsibilities

  • Security Monitoring & Incident Response
    • Monitor security tools, alerts, and system activity to identify potential threats
    • Investigate suspicious events and determine appropriate response actions
    • Coordinate cybersecurity incident response activities, including investigation, containment, recovery, documentation, and follow-up
    • Escalate complex security incidents as needed and track incidents through resolution
  • Threat Detection & Analysis
    • Analyze email security, endpoint protection, and identity-related security alerts
    • Correlate available data to identify potential cybersecurity threats
    • Document findings and recommend or initiate response actions
  • Vulnerability Management
    • Conduct vulnerability scans and analyze findings
    • Prioritize vulnerabilities based on risk, exploitability, and business impact
    • Partner with system owners to communicate risks and remediation recommendations
    • Validate remediation efforts and ensure identified risks are adequately addressed
    • Track remediation activities and escalate unresolved security risks
  • Identity & Access Security
    • Conduct access reviews and evaluate access change requests
    • Administer multifactor authentication (MFA) controls
    • Monitor privileged account activity
    • Identify excessive or inappropriate access and recommend corrective actions
  • Security Operations & Compliance
    • Administer and maintain assigned cybersecurity tools and technologies
    • Troubleshoot security control gaps and recommend improvements
    • Maintain security documentation, inventories, procedures, and records
    • Support security audits, compliance efforts, and control reviews
  • Security Awareness
    • Assist with phishing simulations and employee security awareness initiatives
    • Analyze trends and identify recurring risk patterns
    • Help promote cybersecurity best practices across the organization
  • Continuous Improvement
    • Stay informed about emerging cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, technologies, and industry trends
    • Recommend enhancements to security processes, controls, and technologies
    • Contribute to the ongoing maturity of the cybersecurity program


Qualifications

Required:

  • Associate’s Degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field
  • 2+ years’ work related and/or related military experience
  • Ability to handle and resolve frequent interpersonal conflict
  • Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills with a keen attention to detail
  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft Office products
  • Strong knowledge of computer networking fundamentals and Cybersecurity concepts and best practices
  • Ability to investigate, understand, and document network security architecture
  • Ability to travel up to 10% of the time and work flexible hours
  • Ability to follow all procedures of the company and IT department
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills
  • Ability to handle highly confidential and sensitive information
  • Exceptional communication and negotiation skills to liaise with internal teams and external partners
  • Ability to respond quickly, accurately, and professionally to demands and requests from customers and employees
  • Exemplifies Titan Machinery’s Core Values
  • Demonstrated initiative and sound independent judgment, with the ability to prioritize competing security risks, make timely decisions within established authority, document the rationale for actions, and escalate matters when business impact or complexity warrants leadership review


Preferred:

  • CompTIA Security+
  • ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
  • Microsoft Security Fundamentals (SC-900)


Titan Machinery provides a generous total compensation package including the following:

  • Comprehensive Health and Dental Coverage
  • HSA (Health Savings Account) - up to $1200 tax-free each year, contributed to your account by Titan Machinery
  • 8 Paid Holidays, Competitive PTO, and Paid Company Volunteer Hours
  • 401(k) with company matching on your FIRST DAY of employment 
  • 100% Paid Pregnancy-Related Leave and Parental Bonding
  • Additional Voluntary Benefits such as: Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Short-term Disability, and more!
  • Additional Leave Benefits such as: Bereavement, Volunteer EMT, and Firefighter
  • Performance-based incentives  


Learn more about our benefits here: https://www.titanmachinery.com/titancareers/careers/benefits

Job Description

Everforth ECS is seeking a Senior SOC Analyst to work in a hybrid capacity at our Fairfax, VA office.

The Senior SOC Analyst will play a key part in standing up and operating the program’s Security Operations Center (SOC), including security monitoring, threat hunting, incident analysis, incident response, and SIEM development. This individual will help build the SOC capability from the ground up and will serve as the primary hands-on SOC resource.

The ideal candidate is a highly technical cybersecurity professional who can independently investigate complex alerts and anomalous activity, determine whether events represent legitimate security incidents, and drive confirmed incidents through the full response lifecycle. The Senior SOC Analyst will also help improve detection coverage, incident response processes, documentation, and overall SOC capabilities. The Senior SOC Analyst reports to the Senior Information System Security Manager.

Job Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary SOC resource for a new unclassified AWS environment.
  • Build, configure, tune, and continuously improve SIEM queries, correlation rules, alerts, dashboards, reports, and detection content.
  • Monitor and investigate security alerts, notable events, IoCs, and anomalous activity to determine whether activity is an explained anomaly or a potential cybersecurity incident.
  • Own confirmed cybersecurity incidents from detection through closure, ensuring incident tickets, timelines, findings, response actions, and supporting evidence remain accurate and complete.
  • Perform advanced analysis using endpoint, network, identity, cloud, application, operating system, and other available security telemetry to determine scope, impact, attack vector, and root cause.
  • Coordinate incident response activities with cybersecurity, cloud, network, system administration, application, and other technical teams and ensure participating teams document required actions and evidence.
  • Ensure incident response activities address detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review.
  • Analyze and correlate IoCs, CVEs, threat intelligence, malicious infrastructure, and adversary Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) to determine potential impact and develop appropriate detections, threat hunts, and defensive actions.
  • Apply frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK to support investigations, detection development, and proactive threat hunting.
  • Tune detection logic to improve coverage, identify gaps, and reduce false positives.
  • Develop and maintain SOC SOPs, incident runbooks, escalation procedures, and other supporting operational documentation.
  • Identify opportunities to automate alert enrichment, event correlation, investigation workflows, ticketing, and SOC reporting.
  • Develop SOC metrics and reporting to communicate alert trends, incident activity, response performance, and identified security gaps.
  • Lead post-incident After Action Reports (AARs), documenting the incident timeline, response activities, lessons learned, root cause, and recommended improvements to detections, controls, and response procedures.
  • Mentor junior analysts and provide technical guidance during investigations and incident response activities.
  • Continuously evaluate and improve SOC monitoring, detection, investigation, and incident response capabilities.
  • Other duties, as assigned.

Salary: $130,000-150,000

General Description Of Benefits

Required Skills

  • U.S. Citizen.
  • Ability to obtain Secret clearance (active preferred)
  • Active DoD 8140 IAT Level II Security+ (or higher).
  • Ability to work up to 3 days a week in a hybrid capacity out of Fairfax, VA. Additional onsite support may be required based on operational or mission needs.
  • 8+ years of cybersecurity experience, including 4+ years in a SOC environment.
  • Strong experience with SIEM technologies, including developing queries, correlation rules, alerts, dashboards, reports, and detection logic.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently triage and investigate complex security alerts, notable events, anomalous activity, and potential cybersecurity incidents.
  • Experience owning cybersecurity incidents through the full response lifecycle, including detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and post incident review.
  • Direct experience supporting security monitoring and incident response in AWS environments, including analysis of CloudTrail, CloudWatch, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty, IAM activity, and other AWS security telemetry.
  • Strong understanding of Windows, Linux, networking, cloud infrastructure, endpoint security, applications, identity, and authentication as they relate to security monitoring and incident response.
  • Experience with the following:
    • Analyzing and correlating telemetry from multiple sources, including endpoint, network, identity, cloud, application, and operating system logs.
    • Onboarding and validating log sources to ensure security telemetry is complete, accurate, and usable for monitoring and investigation.
    • Analyzing identity and authentication activity from Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, or similar identity platforms.
    • Analyzing Indicators of Compromise (IoCs), CVEs, suspicious authentication activity, and TTPs.
    • Conducting proactive threat hunts and developing or tuning detections based on observed activity, threat intelligence, and emerging threats.
    • Developing and maintaining SOC procedures, incident response playbooks, runbooks, escalation processes, and operational workflows.
  • Working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK or similar frameworks and experience applying them to investigations, detection development, and threat hunting.
  • Ability to:
    • Lead technical incident response activities, coordinate actions across multiple technical teams, and ensure incident documentation remains accurate and complete.
    • Independently manage SOC operations and prioritize alerts, investigations, incidents, and other operational requirements.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, with a proven ability to weigh the relative costs and benefits of potential actions and identify the most appropriate solution.
  • Highly developed interpersonal and oral/written communication skills, with the ability to effectively and professionally interact with a diverse set of stakeholders (from peers to end-users to executive management)
Desired Skills

  • Advanced cybersecurity certifications such as CISSP, CySA+, GCIH, GCIA, GMON, CEH, or similar certifications.
  • Experience with the following:
    • Supporting cybersecurity operations in DoD, DISA, AWS GovCloud, or other federal environments.
    • Elastic Security, including query development, detection rules, dashboards, alert tuning, and security investigations.
    • Helping stand up or significantly mature a SOC, including development of monitoring, detection, incident response, and operational processes.
    • Monitoring and investigating Kubernetes or containerized environments and working with endpoint security technologies such as Trellix or similar platforms.

Application Close Date

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

The role is part of the In-Space Systems business unit, which is focused on addressing two of the most compelling challenges in spaceflight today: space infrastructure and increasing mobility on-orbit.

Blue National Security (BNS) builds and operates space systems for the Intelligence Community and Department of Defense. Someone has to be watching those systems continuously — and that's this role.

We're looking for a Cyber Defense Analyst to monitor, investigate, and respond across BNS classified enclaves, mission ground systems, and labs. You'll work real events on real national security systems, and you'll do it alongside senior engineers who will teach you the environment rather than hand you a queue and walk away.

This is a hands-on-keyboard role. You'll spend your days in consoles, terminals, and logging data. You'll also get your hands on the tooling itself, helping deploy sensors, onboard log sources, and tune detections under the direction of our senior engineers. That's how you'll learn this environment, and it's the fastest path to becoming the engineer who designs the next one.

If you're coming off a military cyber protection team, a government SOC, or a service watch floor and you want to keep growing technically rather than get slotted into a ticket queue, this is a strong landing spot.

What You'll Do

  • Monitor and triage. Work security events and alerts across SIEM, EDR, network sensors, and audit logs. Determine what's noise, what's misconfiguration, and what warrants escalation.
  • Investigate. Pull the threads — pivot across host, network, and identity data to build a picture of what actually happened, and document it clearly.
  • Respond. Serve as first responder during incidents. Execute containment steps per playbook, preserve evidence, build timelines, and support senior engineers leading the response.
  • Hunt. Participate in structured hunts, initially alongside senior team members and increasingly on your own hypotheses as you learn what "normal" looks like here.
  • Support audit and insider threat review. Perform privileged user activity monitoring and audit log review in partnership with Security and Counterintelligence.
  • Stand watch during mission events. Provide heightened monitoring coverage during launches, mission operations, and other critical windows.
  • Get hands on the tooling. Assist with sensor deployment, log source onboarding, and agent rollout across enclaves under engineering direction.
  • Tune and improve detections. Reduce false positives, validate rule coverage, and propose new detections based on what you find in the data.
  • Improve the playbooks. Execute response procedures and flag every gap you hit — you'll be the first to find them, and your input drives the rewrites.
  • Automate what you repeat. Script recurring triage, enrichment, and reporting tasks. We'll help you build this skill if you don't have it yet.

Required Qualifications

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, incident response, IT operations, or system administration or equivalent military/government cyber experience
  • Working knowledge of network protocols and Windows and Linux fundamentals
  • Familiarity with SIEM and EDR concepts and the ability to investigate events using them
  • Understanding of common attack techniques and exposure to the MITRE ATT&CK framework
  • Clear, concise written communication — your investigation notes will be read by senior staff and government customers
  • Genuine curiosity and the instinct to keep pulling on a thread when something doesn't add up
  • Active U.S. Government Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility and eligibility for SAP access determination; U.S. citizenship
  • DoD 8140 CSSP Analyst or IAT Level II certification (Security+ CE or equivalent) at hire or within [6] months

A degree is not required. Equivalent military, government, or hands-on technical experience is fully accepted.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior military cyber experience (17C, 1B4, CTN, 1721, or equivalent) or CPT/CST assignment
  • Any scripting exposure — Python, PowerShell, or Bash
  • Query language familiarity — KQL, SPL, or similar
  • Prior work in classified DoD or IC environments
  • Exposure to forensics, malware triage, or detection rule development
  • Security+, CySA+, GSEC, GCIH, or similar
  • Active TS/SCI with polygraph

Why This Role

Most early-career defensive cyber jobs are queue jobs. You close tickets, escalate anything interesting, and learn very little about the systems you're supposedly defending.

This team is small enough that you can't be siloed. You'll sit next to the engineers building the enclaves, help deploy the sensors you'll be watching, and see your tuning recommendations go live. When you find a gap during a hunt, you'll be in the room when we decide how to close it.

We're hiring at this level specifically to grow people into senior engineers. If that's the trajectory you want, we'll be explicit about what it takes and invest accordingly.

Logistics

  • Onsite in classified spaces; no telework by nature of the role
  • Heightened coverage expectations during launches and mission-critical events
  • Limited travel, up to 10%
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain access to classified facilities; periodic polygraph may be required

Base Pay Range For

CO applicants is $90,934.00 - $127,307.25 WA applicants is $99,201.00 - $138,880.35

Other Site Ranges May Differ

Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Export Control Regulations

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Background Check

  • Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
  • Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
  • Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
  • Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

  • Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
  • Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
  • Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
  • Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

Protect Critical Healthcare Systems. Defend Patient Data. Drive Security Excellence.

Pivotal Health is seeking an experienced and highly motivated IT Security Analyst to join our growing technology team in Fargo, North Dakota.


As an IT Security Analyst, you will play a vital role in protecting enterprise systems, securing sensitive healthcare data, and strengthening the cybersecurity posture of a national healthcare organization. This position offers the opportunity to work directly with IT leadership, influence security strategy, and help safeguard mission-critical operations across multiple locations.


If you're passionate about cybersecurity, threat detection, vulnerability management, incident response, network security, and regulatory compliance, we'd love to hear from you.


What You'll Do

  • Monitor networks, endpoints, and systems for security threats, vulnerabilities, and suspicious activity

  • Investigate, analyze, and respond to cybersecurity incidents and security alerts

  • Conduct vulnerability assessments and coordinate remediation efforts

  • Maintain and support security technologies, including SIEM, endpoint protection, firewalls, IDS/IPS, and other monitoring tools

  • Assist in implementing cybersecurity controls, security policies, and best practices

  • Support compliance initiatives related to HIPAA and healthcare security requirements

  • Perform risk assessments, security audits, and control reviews

  • Collaborate with infrastructure and application teams to ensure secure system configurations

  • Help develop, maintain, and test incident response and disaster recovery plans

  • Research emerging cybersecurity threats, attack techniques, and industry trends

  • Recommend improvements to strengthen overall organizational security


Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent work experience

  • 3+ years of experience in cybersecurity, information security, or IT security analysis

  • Experience working with security monitoring and SIEM platforms

  • Knowledge of endpoint protection, antivirus, and endpoint detection solutions

  • Experience managing or supporting network security technologies including firewalls and IDS/IPS tools

  • Familiarity with vulnerability scanning, remediation, and threat mitigation processes

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills

  • Ability to investigate, prioritize, and respond effectively to security incidents

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills
