descriptionHtml:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Information security is an integral part of Visa's corporate culture. It is essential to maintaining our position as an industry leader in electronic payments, which is why Visa has made it a priority to create top-tier security operations and incident response teams to defend the company against evolving cyber threats. If you would like to join a company where security is truly valued, where you can work with like-minded peers who are passionate about the art & science of cyber defense, and where you can use state of the art tools for maximum impact, then we have a home for you.

The successful candidate will work with a team of incident responders at one of Visa's Cyber Fusion Centers. The team is part of a larger organization located across multiple geographical sites that are responsible for the comprehensive cyber defense of Visa and its subsidiaries.

Essential Functions

  • Manage and address cybersecurity incidents through all stages, including identification, containment, and eradication.
  • Perform deep-dive analysis on systems, accounts, and networks to identify the root cause and impact of incidents.
  • Act as an engagement point for broader technology teams, including Cyber Defense and Engineering.
  • Perform proactive threat hunting to identify and mitigate potential threats before they can cause harm.
  • Develop and refine detection rules to improve the identification and response to security incidents.
  • Provide detailed reports and documentation of incidents and response actions.
  • Develop and maintain incident response playbooks and runbooks to ensure standardized and efficient response processes.
  • Contribute to identifying process improvement opportunities to enhance security incident response processes.
  • Support and manage cybersecurity projects to enhance overall security posture.

Work Arrangement

This position is staffed in shifts supporting a 24x7x365 global security operations center. Analysts work a series of 12-hour shifts (followed by days off). Staff assigned to the operations center are considered critical and may need to cover holidays and weekends, if scheduled.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree, OR 3+ years of relevant work experience
  • Experience working in an enterprise-level incident response team or security operations center.
  • Professional experience in cybersecurity or computer network defense roles.
  • Experience with GenAI and Agent automation

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in an enterprise-level incident response team or security operations center.
  • Professional experience in cybersecurity or computer network defense roles.
  • Relevant security-related certifications a plus: CISSP, GCIH, GCIA, GCED, GCFA, CySA+.
  • Demonstrated expertise in areas like incident response, intrusion and malware analysis, web application security, or security engineering.
  • Extensive understanding of malware types and network attack methods.
  • Strong grasp of TCP/IP, packet analysis, routing, and network security.
  • Extensive expertise in operating systems (Windows and Linux), as well as network services and applications.
  • Direct experience in handling cyber security incidents and associated incident response tools.
  • Strong working knowledge of common security tools such as SIEM, AV, WAF, IDS, Netflow, Packet Analyzer and Endpoint Detection & Response tools.
  • Understanding of web application security vulnerabilities, such as cross-site scripting, cross-site request forgery, SQL injection, denial-of-service attacks, and API attacks.
  • Good understanding of Web Application Security risks.
  • Excellent understanding of DDoS techniques and mitigation mechanisms.
  • Display great problem-solving skills, with tenacity and resilience to resolve issues.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills with proven skill in presenting analytical data effectively to varied audiences.
  • Strong interpersonal and leadership skills to influence and build credibility as a peer.
  • Strong understanding of cloud technologies and related security best practices.

Information for US Applicants

For roles located in the US, the estimated salary range for this position is $84,500.00 to $ 131,400.00 USD per year, which may include potential sales incentive payments (if applicable). Salary may vary depending on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location. In addition, this position may be eligible for bonus and equity.Visa has a comprehensive benefits package for which this position may be eligible that includes Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), FSA/HSA, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, and Wellness Program.

Work Hours

Varies upon the needs of the department.

Travel Requirements

This position requires travel 5-10% of the time.

Mental/Physical Requirements

This position will be performed in an office setting. The position will require the incumbent to sit and stand at a desk, communicate in person and by telephone, frequently operate standard office equipment, such as telephones and computers.

Visa is an EEO Employer

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protect veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

About AbbVie

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

Job Description

This position is part of AbbVie’s Information Security & Risk Management (ISRM) team. We are here to put our partners in a position to succeed. We do it by providing the knowledge, tools, and support they need to effectively use data and technology while also effectively managing risk. AbbVie Information Security is looking for a highly motivated, talented defender to join the Cyber Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT).

The Cyber Security Operations Center (CSOC) manages the initial investigation and response to security events, alerts, and threats, and works directly to augment incident responders during critical security events. GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

The Cyber Security Analyst is tasked with proactively safeguarding the organization's information assets and infrastructure against evolving cyber threats. This position involves advanced threat hunting, vulnerability management, security architecture design, and incident response. The analyst will leverage deep networking expertise and a thorough understanding of modern cybersecurity principles to implement robust security measures, ensure regulatory compliance, and continuously improve the organization's security posture.

Essential Functions

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Identify, analyze, and mitigate security risks and threats.
  • Conduct advanced threat hunting to identify and neutralize sophisticated threats using SIEM, EDR, and other tools.
  • Perform vulnerability assessments and penetration testing to remediate security weaknesses.
  • Design and maintain secure network architectures, including firewalls, IDS/IPS, and VPNs.
  • Apply strong networking knowledge (TCP/IP, routing, switching) to enhance security.
  • Manage and maintain an up-to-date inventory of all devices, including servers, workstations, and related network devices, ensuring assets are secure and compliant.
  • Utilize SQL to query, analyze, troubleshoot, and manage databases, including supporting database maintenance, backups, access controls, and performance optimization.
  • Designs security policies, programs, or practices to ensure adequate security relating to asset protection, alarm response, access card use, and other security needs. 
  • Coordinate meetings with stakeholders and vendors to discuss security strategies, review audits, and plan security reviews and improvements.
  • Develop and maintain security policies and procedures, to ensure a secure and resilient IT infrastructure.
  • Develop and lead security awareness training initiatives for employees, emphasizing the importance of security best practices and how to recognize and prevent potential threats.
  • Participate in planning and executing disaster recovery and business continuity plans, ensuring the availability and integrity of critical systems and databases in the event of a cyber incident.

MINIMUM EDUCATION AND TRAINING

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field
  • Minimum of five (5) years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, with a focus on threat hunting, incident response, and network security.
  • Possess or be able to obtain CompTIA Security+ and Network+ certifications. CompTIA CySA+ certification is preferred.
  • An equivalent combination of education and experience with provide the requisite knowledge , skills, and abilities for the job will be considered.

Minimum Qualifications And Standards Required

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Experience with SQL and scripting languages (Python, PowerShell, etc.) is a plus.
  • Advanced knowledge of cybersecurity principles, frameworks, and best practices.
  • Expertise in threat-hunting methodologies, techniques, and tools (e.g., SIEM, EDR, threat intelligence platforms).
  • Strong understanding of network security principles, protocols, and technologies.
  • Proficiency in vulnerability management, penetration testing, and security assessment tools.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.  
  • Experience with cloud security (AWS, Azure, GCP) is preferred

Physical Requirements

This role involves moderate physical activity, including occasional movement through data centers and secure facilities that may require lifting objects of moderate weight (up to 20 pounds). The position may involve working in diverse conditions, including exposure to controlled environments (e.g., data centers with variable climates, electrical hazards, and other physical factors). Occasional travel may be required.

descriptionHtml:
Brief Description

The Rudolph Libbe Group is a leading, full-service provider of construction and facility solutions headquartered in Walbridge, Ohio. Founded in 1955, RLG operates as a single-source partner for clients across diverse industries, offering expertise in construction management, design-build, energy solutions, and ongoing facility maintenance.

Our organization is comprised of multiple companies working together as one team. This integrated structure allows us to deliver everything from site selection and financing to construction, renovation, and long-term facility management, ensuring seamless service and exceptional results. At RLG, we pride ourselves on a safety-first culture, collaborative approach, and commitment to quality, making us one of the top contractors in the nation.

The Information Security Analyst helps protect the organization’s information systems and data. Working under close supervision, this role supports security monitoring, incident response, risk assessments, compliance, and remediation while building foundational cybersecurity knowledge. You’ll collaborate with IS colleagues and internal stakeholders to document findings, support security tools, and strengthen safe computing practices across the organization.

Job Responsibilities

  • Monitor security alerts and escalate potential threats according to established procedures.
  • Assist with incident containment, documentation, and post-incident analysis.
  • Support endpoint, email, and network security monitoring activities.
  • Assist with audits, vulnerability assessments, risk evaluations, and remediation efforts.
  • Help assess adherence to internal controls, data protection standards, applicable laws, and security policies.
  • Support the operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and evaluation of antivirus, SIEM, vulnerability management, and endpoint security tools.
  • Help prepare security reports, findings summaries, and recommendations; maintain accurate records of incidents, risks, and control assessments.
  • Maintain security diagrams, procedures, support documentation, ticket notes, and knowledge base contributions.
  • Assist with user education, phishing awareness, and safe computing practices.
  • Participate in training and hands-on learning, and apply feedback and lessons learned to improve security practices.

Skills

  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication.
  • Ability to follow technical instructions, ask clarifying questions, and document key information accurately.
  • Foundational analytical and problem-solving skills to assess alerts, vulnerabilities, and audit findings.
  • Good judgment in recognizing potential security risks and escalating them appropriately.
  • Reliability, accountability, and attention to detail when completing assigned work.
  • Collaborative approach when working with IS colleagues and internal stakeholders.
  • Commitment to protecting confidential information and acting ethically.
  • Curiosity and willingness to learn about cybersecurity tools, threats, and best practices.

Education/Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Entry-level experience (0–2 years), an internship, or academic exposure to security concepts preferred.
  • Customer service or technical support experience beneficial.
  • Experience with SIEM’s, firewalls, VPNs, IDS’s, AV, EDR, email security is desirable.
  • Security certifications such as CompTIA Security+ are preferred.



Interested parties should apply on our website at www.rlgbuilds.com/careers.

The Rudolph/Libbe Companies, Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer.

Detection Engineering & Automation:



Develop, implement, and optimize detection logic, playbooks, and automated response workflows to reduce mean time to containment and improve SOC efficiency.



Process Improvement:



Continuously assess and enhance SOC processes and procedures, ensuring best practices and alignment with evolving threat landscapes.



Threat Intelligence Integration:



Collaborate with threat intelligence teams to analyze emerging risks and integrate relevant TTPs (Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures) into SOC operations.



Stakeholder Engagement:



Act as a trusted advisor to internal stakeholders, translating technical findings into actionable insights and ensuring transparency throughout security operations.



Compliance & Governance:



Ensure all SOC activities comply with relevant standards (e.g., NCSC, Cyber Essentials Plus) and internal Pearson policies.



Reporting & Metrics:



Deliver executive-level reporting, risk assessments, and metrics to demonstrate the effectiveness of SOC operations.

  • Must have experience working with regulated environments or government clients.


  • Proven experience in security operations, incident response, and detection engineering


  • Hands-on expertise with SOAR, EDR, NDR, and SIEM technologies


  • Experience with one or more Cloud Service Providers (AWS, Azure, GCP)


  • Strong background in multitasking, adapting, and thriving in fast-paced environments


  • Excellent communication skills, especially in stakeholder management and translating technical risk to non-technical audiences

  • US – Strong understanding of FedRAMP, GovRAMP and StateRAMP policies and practices.

Job Number: R0252812

Cybersecurity Operations Center Analyst, Senior

The Opportunity:

Are you ready to take a strategic role in cyber defense? Are you looking for an opportunity to protect critical infrastructure from the constant onslaught of cyber-attacks? If you want to sharpen your skills by analyzing threats in real-time, you want to be a Cybersecurity Operations Center Analyst.

As a Cybersecurity Operations Center Analyst on our security operations center team, you’ll improve tier monitoring strategies and analyze threats, using state-of-the-art tools and platforms. You’ll work with the team to comprehend, mitigate, and respond to threats quickly, restoring operations and limiting the impact. You’ll manage efforts to figure out just how many systems are affected and assist recovery efforts. You’ll combine threat intelligence, event data, and assessments of events to identify patterns to understand attackers’ goals to stop them from succeeding. This is a great opportunity to continue to build your cybersecurity skills with hands-on experience in threat assessment and incident response. Join us as we protect clients from malicious actors.

In this role, you’ll lead a team of professionals as they use cyberspace capabilities to evaluate potential weaknesses as well as the effectiveness of mitigations for cybersecurity solutions. You will leverage cyberspace operations systems to aggregate threat feeds that inform briefings for senior leadership aligned to our Army client.

If you want to be in the fight, working shoulder to shoulder with our mission partner influencing the most critical global cyber missions, this is the opportunity for you.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:  

  • 7+ years of experience working in a Security Operations Center (SOC) at a classified level within the DoW
  • Experience leading every phase of the incident lifecycle, including conducting rapid triage to determine severity, performing deep-dive investigations into root causes, and assessing appropriate containment, eradication, and remediation strategies to halt active threats
  • Experience working with cybersecurity staff to evolve continuous monitoring toolsets by generating new detection rules and refining existing alerts to maximize high-fidelity alerts and minimize false positives
  • Experience refining, developing, and maturing standard operating procedures (SOPs) and SOC responsibilities throughout each stage of the incident response lifecycle
  • Ability to manage post-compromise activities, focusing on the eradication of malicious artifacts, guiding the secure recovery of mission services, and generating comprehensive After-Action Reports (AARs) to document lessons learned
  • Ability to serve as a primary focal point for active incident response operations, taking responsibility for technical coordination and clear communication with key stakeholders
  • TS/SCI clearance
  • HS diploma or GED
  • Ability to obtain an 8570 DoW approved CSSP baseline Certification such as CEH, CFR, CCNA Cyber Ops, CCNA-Security, CySA+, GCIA, GCIH, GICSP, Cloud+, SCYBER, or PenTest+ Certification, prior to start date


Nice If You Have:  

  • Experience using Elastic for monitoring, analysis, and case management
  • Experience using endpoint tools to successfully hunt for adversarial behavior
  • Experience with GCFA, GNFA, or equivalent digital forensics
  • Ability to conduct threat hunting using network and host-based information
  • TS/SCI clearance with a polygraph
  • 8570 CSSP Analyst or Incident Responder Certification


Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; TS/SCI clearance is required.

Compensation

At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $99,000.00 to $225,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date.

Identity Statement

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

Candidate AI Usage Policy

AI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided.

Work Model

Our people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.

  • Remote: If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.
  • Hybrid: If this position is listed as hybrid, you will be expected to work from a Booz Allen or customer facility, in alignment with your leadership's expectations and the needs of the role.
  • Onsite: If this position is listed as onsite, work will primarily be performed full-time at a customer facility, where employees will collaborate directly with colleagues and customers as required by the role.


Commitment to Non-Discrimination

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local, or international law.

Application Instructions

Sterling Infrastructure is looking for a SR Security Analyst to join their growing IT Team!

About The Role

Sterling Infrastructure is continuing to mature its cybersecurity program. We are looking for a Senior Security Analyst to serve as the technical lead for incident response across Sterling and its operating companies.

In this role, you will lead the technical response to significant security incidents, from initial triage and investigation through containment, recovery, and post-incident review. You will work closely with the Cybersecurity team, our managed detection and response (MDR) partner, and IT teams across the organization.

This is a hands-on role for someone who has independently handled complex security incidents, can make sound decisions with incomplete information, remains composed under pressure, and wants to help strengthen the incident response capabilities of a growing cybersecurity program.

Position Description

What You'll Do

Incident Response | Primary Focus

    • Lead significant security incidents from initial triage through scoping, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review; provide escalation support and oversight for lower-severity incidents.
    • Investigate email, identity, and business email compromise (BEC) incidents across Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, including sign-in activity, authentication changes, mailbox access, mail-flow activity, OAuth and application activity, and persistence mechanisms.
    • Perform forensic triage of endpoints and servers using memory, disk, EDR, and log artifacts, and coordinate deeper forensic analysis when required.
    • Serve as the technical escalation point for alerts and investigations from our MDR partner and coordinate response activities with affected Cybersecurity and IT teams.
    • Build, maintain, and continuously improve the incident response plan, severity matrix, technical response procedures, and incident-specific playbooks.
    • Develop scripts, queries, and repeatable workflows to automate evidence collection, enrichment, incident scoping, and common response activities.
    • Plan and facilitate tabletop exercises for both technical teams and leadership to validate response procedures and identify opportunities for improvement.
    • Preserve forensic evidence and maintain appropriate evidence-handling and chain-of-custody documentation.
    • Produce clear incident reports, investigation findings, timelines, and briefings for both technical teams and leadership.
    • Track and analyze incident response metrics, including time to detect, time to contain, time to recover, incident trends, and recurring root causes.
    • Identify lessons learned from incidents and work with appropriate teams to improve controls, detection capabilities, and response procedures.
Detection and Threat Hunting

    • Develop and tune SIEM searches, queries, and detections based on observed attacker techniques and organizational risk.
    • Map detection coverage and identified gaps to MITRE ATT&CK where appropriate.
    • Conduct targeted threat hunts using threat intelligence, observed indicators, attacker behaviors, and lessons learned from previous incidents.
    • Identify logging, telemetry, and visibility gaps that affect detection or investigation capabilities and work with appropriate teams to address them.
    • Translate findings from incidents and threat hunts into improved detections and investigation procedures.
Program Support

    • Validate organizational exposure to actively exploited and high-risk vulnerabilities and provide risk-based remediation recommendations to vulnerability management and infrastructure teams.
    • Support cybersecurity assessments of newly acquired companies and help integrate them into Sterling's security monitoring, detection, and incident response processes.
    • Mentor other security analysts through shared investigations, technical reviews, knowledge transfer, and runbook development.
    • Contribute to the continued maturity of Sterling's security operations and incident response capabilities.
Position Requirements

What You Bring - Required

    • 5+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, or digital forensics, including at least 3 years independently leading security investigations and response activities.
    • Demonstrated experience leading complex security incidents, making containment recommendations with incomplete information, and coordinating technical response across multiple teams.
    • Strong Microsoft 365 and Entra ID investigation skills, including Entra sign-in and audit logs, Microsoft Purview audit logs, mailbox activity and rules, authentication methods, Conditional Access, and related identity activity.
    • Practical experience investigating business email compromise, account takeover, phishing, credential theft, and other identity-based attacks.
    • Hands-on experience with enterprise EDR and SIEM platforms, including the ability to develop and troubleshoot your own investigative queries.
    • Experience performing endpoint and server forensic triage using EDR telemetry, Windows event logs, memory, disk, and other available forensic artifacts.
    • Solid understanding of Windows internals, Active Directory, authentication, and networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, firewalls, and VPN technologies.
    • Working knowledge of common attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.
    • Scripting skills in PowerShell or Python with the ability to automate evidence collection, data analysis, enrichment, or repetitive investigation tasks.
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to distinguish confirmed findings from assumptions and identify gaps in available evidence.
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical findings, risk, and incident impact clearly to both technical teams and leadership.
    • Ability to remain composed and make sound technical decisions during high-pressure security incidents.
    • Willingness to participate in the cybersecurity on-call rotation and respond after hours when required during active incidents.
Preferred

    • Certifications such as GCIH, GCFA, GCFE, or GNFA.
    • Experience investigating incidents in complex, multi-company, decentralized, or M&A environments with mixed technology and security tool stacks.
    • Experience working with managed detection and response providers and coordinating investigations between internal and external security teams.
    • Experience developing or facilitating cybersecurity incident response tabletop exercises.
Education

    • Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information technology, or equivalent combination of professional experience, training, and education.
Equal Opportunity Employer

We are an equal opportunity employer: We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, genetic information, marital status, military status, membership or activity in a local human rights commission, or status with regard to public assistance, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Incident Response | Primary Focus



- 

- Lead significant security incidents from initial triage through scoping, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review; provide escalation support and oversight for lower-severity incidents.
- Investigate email, identity, and business email compromise (BEC) incidents across Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, including sign-in activity, authentication changes, mailbox access, mail-flow activity, OAuth and application activity, and persistence mechanisms.

- Serve as the technical escalation point for alerts and investigations from our MDR partner and coordinate response activities with affected Cybersecurity and IT teams.
- Build, maintain, and continuously improve the incident response plan, severity matrix, technical response procedures, and incident-specific playbooks.
- Develop scripts, queries, and repeatable workflows to automate evidence collection, enrichment, incident scoping, and common response activities.
- Plan and facilitate tabletop exercises for both technical teams and leadership to validate response procedures and identify opportunities for improvement.
- Preserve forensic evidence and maintain appropriate evidence-handling and chain-of-custody documentation.
- Produce clear incident reports, investigation findings, timelines, and briefings for both technical teams and leadership.
- Track and analyze incident response metrics, including time to detect, time to contain, time to recover, incident trends, and recurring root causes.

- 

- Develop and tune SIEM searches, queries, and detections based on observed attacker techniques and organizational risk.
- Map detection coverage and identified gaps to MITRE ATT&CK where appropriate.
- Conduct targeted threat hunts using threat intelligence, observed indicators, attacker behaviors, and lessons learned from previous incidents.
- Identify logging, telemetry, and visibility gaps that affect detection or investigation capabilities and work with appropriate teams to address them.
- Translate findings from incidents and threat hunts into improved detections and investigation procedures.
Program Support



- 

- Validate organizational exposure to actively exploited and high-risk vulnerabilities and provide risk-based remediation recommendations to vulnerability management and infrastructure teams.
- Support cybersecurity assessments of newly acquired companies and help integrate them into Sterling's security monitoring, detection, and incident response processes.
- Mentor other security analysts through shared investigations, technical reviews, knowledge transfer, and runbook development.
- Contribute to the continued maturity of Sterling's security operations and incident response capabilities.

What You Bring - Required



- 

- 5+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, or digital forensics, including at least 3 years independently leading security investigations and response activities.
- Demonstrated experience leading complex security incidents, making containment recommendations with incomplete information, and coordinating technical response across multiple teams.

-

Evocs Overview

EVOCS was founded with a clear purpose: to help businesses operate more effectively, solve complex challenges, and create opportunities for growth through practical expertise and technology solutions.

As an IT consulting firm, we work with our clients to understand their needs, identify the right technologies, and deliver solutions that improve performance and support their business objectives.

Today, EVOCS is a trusted technology partner to a growing number of organizations and industry leaders. Our team combines technical expertise, business understanding, and a commitment to quality to deliver effective solutions and build lasting client relationships based on responsiveness, consistency, and results.

EVOCS Overview

EVOCS's journey began with a mission to empower businesses with advisory expertise, empowered with ideal technologies to provide them with comprehensive solutions to grow and prosper.

Founded by a team of passionate experts, EVOCS has grown into a trusted partner to a growing number of leaders across their respective industries. Our roots in employee-managed operations reflect our commitment to quality, consistency, and client success.

If you enjoy working in a hyper-fast-growing company, are eager to be part of an agile team, and want to be part of our success story, then let's talk!

🎯 Role Overview

As a SOC Analyst L2, you will own escalated incidents from investigation through containment across FortiSIEM, FortiSOAR and Microsoft Defender XDR.

You will be responsible for finding root cause, driving response, sharpening detections and automation, and raising the bar for the L1 analysts who escalate to you.

🧩 What You Will Do

In this role, you will:

Investigation & Hunting

  • Investigate incidents escalated from L1: build the full timeline, determine scope and root cause, and confirm impact
  • Correlate endpoint, identity, email and network telemetry across Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Identity, Defender for Office 365 and FortiGate / FortiSIEM logs
  • Hunt proactively with Defender XDR advanced hunting (KQL) and FortiSIEM searches, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK

Incident Response

  • Lead containment and eradication — device isolation, account disablement, indicator blocking, malicious email purge — coordinating with IT and network teams
  • Write incident reports covering timeline, root cause, actions taken and recommendations; brief client stakeholders on high-severity events
  • Support major incident response and escalate to L3, IR or threat intel when required

Detection Engineering & Automation

  • Build, tune and retire FortiSIEM correlation rules, watchlists and reports to cut false positives and close detection gaps
  • Design and maintain FortiSOAR playbooks for enrichment, triage and automated response
  • Tune Defender policies, custom detections, suppression rules and alert thresholds

Mentorship & Continuous Improvement

  • Act as escalation point and mentor for L1 — review case quality, coach on investigations and update runbooks
  • Track SOC metrics (MTTD, MTTR, false-positive rate) and recommend process improvements

🧠 What You Will Bring

The top candidate will have the following skills:

  • 3–5 years of hands-on experience as an analyst in a Security Operations Center (SOC), including at least 1–2 years at L2 or in incident response — required; IT support or NOC experience alone does not qualify
  • Experience with FortiSIEM (searches, correlation rules, parsers); FortiSOAR (case handling, playbook building); Microsoft Defender XDR and Defender for Endpoint; KQL advanced hunting; MITRE ATT&CK; incident containment
  • Deep networking and security knowledge: TCP/IP, DNS, firewalls (FortiGate a plus), proxies, VPN and packet analysis
  • Experience with Windows and Linux log analysis, Active Directory and Entra ID sign-in logs
  • A passion for turning recurring manual work into tuned detections and automated playbooks
  • An undying concern about detection gaps and threats that slip past the queue
  • Fluent in English (written and spoken) – bilingual or near-native level
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills – this is a client-facing role that involves frequent interaction via email, calls, and meetings

Ideally you have…

  • A degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or a related field
  • Scripting for automation and analysis — Python, PowerShell, REST APIs
  • Experience with Microsoft Sentinel, Defender for Cloud or Defender for Cloud Apps; MSSP or multi-tenant SOC experience
  • Certifications such as Microsoft SC-200, Fortinet FCP / NSE 5 (FortiSIEM or FortiSOAR), CompTIA CySA+, GCIH, GCIA, or BTL1 / BTL2

We are privileged to serve our loyal customer base in our mission to build lasting relationships with our clients based on trust and mutual success. We strive to deliver exceptional quality and consistency through a white-glove approach. By empowering businesses with tailored solutions and insights, we help them achieve their goals and navigate the ever-evolving tech landscape.

The Values We Live By

  • Customer-centric Solutions

  • Integrity & Transparency
  • Data-driven Decision Making

The posting will be active for a minimum of 3 days. The active posting will continue to extend by 3 days until the position is filled.

descriptionHtml:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About The Team

The Security Operations team at Gusto plays a critical role in fortifying Gusto and our customers against sophisticated threats: phishing attacks, insider risks, data loss, and emerging attack techniques. Our distributed team across Eastern and Pacific time zones monitors, investigates, and responds to security events during business hours, with a lightweight rotation for rare after-hours escalation of critical incidents.

We're looking for a Security Operations analyst with 5+ years of experience to own and deliver security operations projects, take an active role in incident response, and raise the bar for how our team detects and responds to threats. You'll work across our multi-cloud environment (AWS, GCP, and others), build Python-based automation, and help govern the fastest-growing part of our attack surface: non-human identities and AI/agent connections. You'll be the directly responsible individual for medium-sized initiatives, work closely with senior analysts, and help mentor newer teammates.

Here's what you'll do

Own security operations projects end to end. Take medium-sized initiatives (typically 1-2 months, often spanning multiple teams) from problem definition through design, rollout, and measurement. Break down ambiguous goals into deliverables, set expectations with stakeholders, communicate progress and risks, and drive work to completion.

Lead and participate in incident response. Triage, investigate, and respond to security incidents across our cloud and corporate environments. Serve as a core responder, document root cause and remediation, write or contribute to post-mortems, and own the completion of post-mortem action items so lessons turn into lasting improvements.

Improve detection and monitoring. Monitor and triage alerts from tools like AWS GuardDuty/Security Hub/WAF, GCP Security Command Center, and our CSPM platform. Tune and improve detections, reduce noise, and recommend configuration and process improvements based on what you learn from investigations.

Build security operations automation. Write Python to extend our automation frameworks and SOAR playbooks, reducing manual work and improving response times. Own the quality, testing, and documentation of what you ship.

Threat hunting. Hunt for threats across our multi-cloud and corporate environments using threat intelligence and the team's playbooks, and turn findings into new detections or playbooks.

Non-human identity and agentic AI governance (roughly one-third of your time). Help govern machine identities, service accounts, and MCP/agent connections that now outnumber human accounts. Drive improvements such as expanding DLP/Nightfall policy coverage for AI and MCP-connected tools, attributing and cleaning up unowned cloud secrets and service accounts, and moving our MCP review process from reactive intake to proactive, risk-based governance.

AI-assisted security operations. Use AI-assisted tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Claude Skills, MCP-connected tools) to work faster on querying, investigating, and drafting, and apply sound judgment about risks specific to AI tooling, such as prompt injection, data exfiltration through connected tools, and over-permissioned agents. Help set team norms for reviewing and validating AI-assisted work.

Collaborate and mentor. Partner with analyzing, IT, and product teams to support secure practices and communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Mentor newer teammates, share what you learn through documentation and knowledge sharing, and contribute to hiring by interviewing candidates.

Participate in the on-call rotation. This is a business-hours role with a lightweight on-call rotation for rare after-hours escalations, not a 24/7 pager rotation. You'll join the roster (currently about one week per month, shifting to roughly every 5-6 weeks as the team grows), respond to security incidents, and follow through on post-mortem action items afterward.

Here's what we're looking for

Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in security operations, incident response, SOC analysis, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience leading or serving as the primary owner of a project or initiative, including coordinating with other teams.
  • Hands-on experience responding to security incidents, including investigation, root cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.
  • Working knowledge of security monitoring, incident response, and vulnerability management.
  • Familiarity with core cloud security services across major providers (AWS, GCP, or similar) and cloud security fundamentals.
  • Comfortable working in Linux environments.
  • Proficiency in Python for scripting and automation.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise security tools (SIEM, EDR, SOAR, DLP). Deploying or architecting these tools from scratch is not expected at this level.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to communicate findings clearly and escalate appropriately.
  • Comfortable using AI-assisted tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Claude Skills, MCP-connected tools), with a working understanding of AI-specific security risks (prompt injection, data exfiltration via connected tools/MCPs, over-permissioned agents) and how to mitigate them.
  • Familiarity with identity and access concepts (service accounts, API keys/tokens, OAuth) and curiosity about how AI agents and MCP-connected tools introduce new identity and access risk. Deep specialist experience is not expected at this level.
  • Willingness and ability to participate in a lightweight, business-hours-oriented on-call rotation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with log analysis or digital forensics in cloud or on-premise environments.
  • Experience with incident response involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Experience writing or improving detections and playbooks.
  • Familiarity with common vulnerability classes and remediation approaches.
  • Exposure to CI/CD security concepts (e.g., dependency scanning tools like GitHub Dependabot).
  • Familiarity with common security frameworks (e.g., NIST, SOC 2).
  • Experience with identity and access management, non-human identity, secrets management, or MCP/agent architecture.
  • Experience mentoring or onboarding teammates.
  • Security certifications (e.g., Security+, GSEC) are a plus. Advanced certifications (CISSP, CISM, etc.) are not expected at this level.

Compensation

Our cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $147,000-164,000 in Denver, $178,000-199,000 in New York and San Francisco Bay Area. Stock equity is additional. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you.

Gusto takes security and protection of your personal information very seriously. Please review our Fraudulent Activity Disclaimer.

Personal information collected and processed as part of your Gusto application will be subject to Gusto's Applicant Privacy Notice.

Job Description

Position Summary

The Security Operations Analyst supports the detection, investigation, response, and continuous improvement of cybersecurity capabilities across enterprise environments. The role monitors security events, conducts initial investigations, supports incident response, contributes to detection and security engineering, and helps develop operational efficiencies through automation and AI-assisted processes.

The ideal candidate is analytical, technically curious, process-oriented, and eager to develop practical cybersecurity and AI-enabled operations expertise. This individual uses approved AI tools as an analyst accelerator, validates generated outputs, documents assumptions, and escalates decisions or risks that require senior review.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate demonstrates sound judgment, attention to detail, a learning mindset, and ownership of assigned work. They can follow established procedures, communicate findings clearly, experiment responsibly with automation and AI, and contribute to tuning AI agents and advancing AI SOC initiatives under the guidance of senior analysts and engineering teams.

Responsibilities

Security Monitoring, Detection & Incident Response

  • Monitor security platforms, dashboards, alerts, and operational reporting channels for potential cybersecurity threats and operational incidents.
  • Review, triage, investigate, and validate alerts generated by SIEM, EDR, DLP, IAM, network, email, cloud, and other monitoring technologies.
  • Use approved AI-assisted capabilities to summarize alerts, enrich cases, correlate evidence, develop investigative leads, and improve response speed while validating outputs against source data.
  • Execute established incident response playbooks, operational procedures, escalation paths, and human-review requirements.
  • Support evidence collection, documentation, containment activities, case tracking, remediation coordination, and incident closure.
  • Escalate incidents, uncertain AI outputs, access concerns, or decisions requiring advanced analysis to senior analysts and response teams.
  • Maintain situational awareness of active incidents, emerging threats, and operational risks during assigned shifts.

Threat Analysis, Hunting & AI-Augmented Detection Engineering

  • Correlate endpoint, network, identity, cloud, application, and security telemetry to identify indicators of compromise and suspicious activity.
  • Assist in identifying attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures through investigative analysis, threat intelligence, and behavioral context.
  • Use OSINT, threat intelligence feeds, approved AI tools, and operational reporting to support investigations and improve threat visibility.
  • Support hypothesis-driven threat hunting to identify emerging risks and previously undetected malicious behavior.
  • Assist in developing, tuning, testing, and maintaining detection content, alert logic, analytics rules, dashboards, and use cases.
  • Use AI as a supervised aid for query development, alert clustering, detection documentation, false-positive review, and coverage-gap analysis.
  • Identify recurring attack patterns, false positives, telemetry gaps, and opportunities to improve detection effectiveness.
  • Develop working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK, threat modeling, NIST incident response concepts, and modern detection methodologies.

Security Engineering, Automation & AI Agent Operations

  • Support deployment, configuration, maintenance, and optimization of security operations technologies and integrations.
  • Support SOAR, workflow automation, orchestration, and AI-assisted security operations initiatives.
  • Use scripting, query languages, APIs, and automation tools to improve investigation workflows, reporting, enrichment, and repeatable operational tasks.
  • Assist senior analysts and engineers with configuring, testing, and tuning AI agents for defined SecOps use cases such as triage, enrichment, knowledge retrieval, reporting, threat hunting, and detection support.
  • Help refine agent instructions, retrieval content, context, tool access, guardrails, escalation logic, and evaluation of test cases within approved boundaries.
  • Record agent errors, unsupported claims, inconsistent results, access issues, and workflow failures; provide structured feedback for tuning and improvement.
  • Validate AI-agent outputs against authoritative telemetry and case evidence before they are used in investigations or operational decisions.
  • Collaborate with engineering and security teams to improve visibility, strengthen controls, and evaluate emerging AI-driven security capabilities.

AI SOC Innovation & Continuous Improvement

  • Contribute to AI SOC initiatives by helping identify repeatable analyst pain points, candidate use cases, automation opportunities, and measurable success criteria.
  • Participate in proofs of concept, controlled pilots, user acceptance testing, agent evaluations, and post-deployment feedback activities.
  • Help document AI-enabled workflows, expected outputs, known limitations, human-review steps, escalation paths, and fallback procedures.
  • Provide analyst feedback on usability, trust, accuracy, efficiency, and operational risk to improve AI SOC capabilities.
  • Demonstrate responsible experimentation, professional accountability, and willingness to learn from testing and operational outcomes.

Documentation, Communication & Collaboration

  • Produce incident summaries, investigation reports, shift handoffs, operational updates, and concise AI evaluation findings.
  • Communicate technical findings, confidence, limitations, and recommended next steps to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Support metrics for detection quality, investigation speed, automation reliability, agent accuracy, analyst adoption, and program effectiveness.
  • Partner with security, infrastructure, engineering, risk, privacy, legal, and business teams as appropriate to support cybersecurity and AI SOC initiatives.

Qualifications

  • 1-3 years of experience in Security Operations, Incident Response, IT Operations, Security Engineering, or a related cybersecurity environment.
  • Experience monitoring, triaging, investigating, and escalating security events using established operational processes.
  • Experience supporting incident response and documenting investigations through closure.
  • Ability to work independently on assigned tasks while collaborating effectively within a team and escalating when appropriate.
  • Foundational understanding of security operations, threat detection, incident response, security engineering, and responsible use of automation or AI.
  • Working knowledge of networking, authentication, operating systems, cloud technologies, and enterprise security controls.
  • Familiarity with Windows, Linux/Unix, macOS, and cloud computing platforms.
  • Experience with technologies such as SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, DLP, SOAR, email security, IAM, vulnerability management, and log analysis platforms.
  • Understanding of indicators of compromise, attack methodologies, detection logic, and basic malware concepts.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, collaboration, prioritization, and documentation skills.
  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
